summary.ar: دورات صيفية بمستوى البكالوريوس والماجستير ودورات في اللغة النرويجية في أوسلو بتاريخ يمتد 80 عاماً، مع منح تغطي الرسوم واختيارياً السكن والوجبات وبطاقة النقل لمتقدمي مقررات الماجستير من خارج الاتحاد الأوروبي والمنطقة الاقتصادية الأوروبية.

about.en:
The University of Oslo's International Summer School (ISS), celebrating 80 years, brings students from around the world to Oslo for three- and four-week bachelor's and master's-level courses starting 28 June 2027 and six-week Norwegian language courses starting 21 June 2027. Courses carry credits and ISS housing includes a room, meals, an Oslo travel card and a social programme.

ISS offers scholarships for master's-level courses, chosen on academic and professional achievement, financial need, geographical distribution and diversity. A Basic Fee Scholarship covers tuition and the participation fee; an ISS Accommodation Scholarship also covers shared housing, meals and an Oslo travel card. Citizens of EU/EEA/Switzerland, US and Canadian citizens (who have separate schemes), bachelor's and Norwegian-course applicants and former recipients are not eligible for the general scholarships, so it suits students from countries such as Georgia or Qatar.

en: Credit courses at bachelor's and master's level in Oslo
Scholarships covering tuition, housing, meals and local travel
Norwegian language courses A1–B2

eligibility.en: University students meeting the course's academic requirements and English proficiency; scholarships only for master's-level course applicants who are not EU/EEA/Swiss, US or Canadian citizens or Norwegian residents. All other nationalities can apply.

en: Pick up to two 2027 summer courses on the ISS course list
Apply in Søknadsweb from 4 January 2027 and tick the 'stipend' option for a scholarship
Upload the scholarship form, CV, recommendation letter, transcripts and English proof by 25 January 2027
Self-financed applicants apply by 1 March 2027

costs.en: 2026 fees for non-EU/EEA students: tuition NOK 15,800–21,900, participation fee NOK 3,100, ISS housing (room, meals, travel card) NOK 27,300; 2027 fees to be updated. Scholarships cover tuition and participation fee, optionally housing; travel to Oslo not covered.

score_reason: Funded summer school (tuition plus housing) open to non-EU students including Georgians and Qataris; 2027 dates set.

summary.ka: ინგლისურენოვანი ერთ- და ორკვირიანი კურსები საბუნებისმეტყველო მეცნიერებებსა და ტექნოლოგიებში, სოციალურ და ჰუმანიტარულ მეცნიერებებში ესტონეთის წამყვან უნივერსიტეტში, კულტურული პროგრამით. განაცხადის საფასური 25 ევრო.
summary.ar: دورات بالإنجليزية لمدة أسبوع أو أسبوعين في العلوم والتكنولوجيا والعلوم الاجتماعية والإنسانيات في أبرز جامعة إستونية، مع برنامج ثقافي. رسوم التقديم 25 يورو.

about.en:
UniTartu Summer School brings students and lifelong learners to the University of Tartu for English-taught courses, mostly in the compact student city of Tartu. In 2026 it offered 13 courses in science and technology (for example synthetic biology and self-driving cars), social sciences (such as disinformation) and the arts and humanities, each lasting one or two weeks, plus a social and cultural programme exploring Estonia.

The 2027 edition runs 2–13 August 2027, with courses added through the autumn and the full list by early January 2027. Each application costs a non-refundable EUR 25 (covering up to two programmes); course fees are listed on each course page. Sign up for the newsletter to hear about the application period and early-bird discount.

en: English-taught courses in tech, social sciences and humanities
One- or two-week formats in a student city
Low EUR 25 application fee; early-bird discount

eligibility.en: University students and lifelong learners; each course lists its own admission requirements. All nationalities.

en: Check the UniTartu Summer School page from early January 2027 for the course list
Choose up to two courses and check their requirements and fees
Apply in the application period and pay the EUR 25 application fee by the deadline
Pay the course fee after admission

costs.en: Application fee EUR 25 (non-refundable, covers up to two programmes); course fees vary by course; optional cultural events extra.

score_reason: Affordable, friendly summer school; 2027 details still being added.

name.ar: كلية إيوا الصيفية الدولية (EISC) 2027

duration.ar: نحو 4 أسابيع (الدورة الأولى، أواخر يونيو – يوليو) أو أسبوعان (الدورة الثانية، أغسطس 2027)

summary.en: A co-ed international summer college at Ewha in Seoul: 3-credit English-taught courses on Korea and many other subjects plus four levels of Korean language, for university students and admitted freshmen.
summary.ka: საერთაშორისო საზაფხულო კოლეჯი ევჰას უნივერსიტეტში, სეულში (ქალებისა და მამაკაცებისთვის): 3-კრედიტიანი ინგლისურენოვანი კურსები კორეასა და სხვა თემებზე და კორეული ენის ოთხი დონე, უნივერსიტეტის სტუდენტებისა და ჩარიცხული აბიტურიენტებისთვის.
summary.ar: كلية صيفية دولية مختلطة في جامعة إيوا بسيول: مقررات بثلاث ساعات معتمدة بالإنجليزية عن كوريا ومجالات أخرى وأربعة مستويات من اللغة الكورية، لطلاب الجامعات والمقبولين الجدد.

about.en:
The Ewha International Summer College (EISC) is run by Ewha Womans University's Office of International Affairs and is open to students of all genders. Session 1 (about four weeks) lets fee-paying visiting students take one or two 3-credit courses (45 hours each), taught in English, plus Korean language at four levels; Session 2 is a shorter August session. Optional housing and field trips are available.

It is open to undergraduate and graduate students at accredited universities (minimum GPA 2.0/4.0) and to prospective freshmen already admitted to college. Credits are transcripted by Ewha; transfer depends on your home institution.

en: 3-credit English-taught courses in central Seoul
Korean language at four levels
Early-bird discount; optional dorm and field trips

eligibility.en: Undergraduate or graduate students at an accredited university (cumulative GPA at least 2.0/4.0) and admitted freshmen. All nationalities.

en: Check summer.ewha.ac.kr for 2027 dates and courses
Apply online with passport bio page and transcript/admission proof
Pay the KRW 100,000 application fee (and tuition early for the early-bird discount)
Pay tuition and housing after acceptance; Session 1 deadline about mid-May

costs.en: 2026: application fee KRW 100,000; tuition KRW 1,800,000 (1 course) or 3,000,000 (2 courses) in Session 1, with early-bird reductions; dormitory KRW 730,000–1,300,000; optional field trip about KRW 450,000.

score_reason: Established Seoul summer college; dates estimated from 2026.

summary.ka: დაახლოებით 150 ინგლისურენოვანი მოკლე კურსი, რომლებსაც მსოფლიოს წამყვანი მკვლევრები ჰოკაიდოს უნივერსიტეტის პროფესორებთან ერთად ასწავლიან, მათ შორის საველე სკოლები ჰოკაიდოზე. სტუდენტებისთვის სწავლის ძალიან დაბალი საფასური.
summary.ar: نحو 150 مقرراً قصيراً باللغة الإنجليزية يدرّسها باحثون عالميون بالتعاون مع أساتذة جامعة هوكايدو، بما فيها مدارس ميدانية في أنحاء هوكايدو، برسوم دراسية منخفضة جداً للطلاب.

about.en:
Since 2016 Hokkaido University has run the Hokkaido Summer Institute (HSI), bringing world-leading researchers to Sapporo to teach short courses with HU faculty. Around 150 English-taught courses run between June and October, attended by 750+ students from overseas universities and 1,500 HU students, in fields from marine biology, veterinary medicine and Antarctic science to tourism, gender studies, sustainability and Japanese culture, many with field training.

University and graduate students enrolled as degree students can take courses for 1 or 2 credits. Tuition for students is just JPY 14,800 per 1-credit course (JPY 29,600 for 2 credits), plus a JPY 1,500 system fee, though some field courses add accommodation and travel costs. HSI offers no scholarships of its own.

en: ~150 English-taught courses with international researchers
Field schools across Hokkaido
Very affordable tuition for students (JPY 14,800 per credit-course)

eligibility.en: Students enrolled as degree students at a university or graduate school at the time of application and during the course; working adults can join non-credit professional courses. All nationalities.

en: Check the HSI site from late January 2027 for courses and application windows
Create an account, choose courses and upload documents in an application window
Pay the JPY 1,500 system usage fee by credit card
After acceptance, pay tuition, book accommodation and arrange insurance/visa

costs.en: Students: JPY 14,800 (1-credit) or JPY 29,600 (2-credit) tuition per course plus JPY 1,500 system fee (2025/26 rates); some field courses have extra costs. No HSI scholarships.

score_reason: Huge course choice at a top Japanese university for very low fees.

name.ar: الجامعة الصيفية في جامعة آرهوس 2027

duration.ka: 3-კვირიანი ტერმები (2027 წლის 5–23 ივლისი ან 26 ივლისი – 13 აგვისტო)
duration.ar: فصول من 3 أسابيع (5–23 يوليو أو 26 يوليو – 13 أغسطس 2027)

deadline_note: Aarhus University: summer 2027 Term 1 is 5–23 July and Term 2 is 26 July – 13 August; application period 15 January – 10 March 2027 (12 noon CET).

summary.en: 85+ English-taught courses worth 5 or 10 ECTS across all academic areas at a top-100 university in Denmark, with a lively social programme. Free for nominated partner students; modest fees for freemovers.
summary.ka: 85-ზე მეტი ინგლისურენოვანი კურსი 5 ან 10 ECTS კრედიტით ყველა აკადემიურ სფეროში დანიის top-100 უნივერსიტეტში, აქტიური სოციალური პროგრამით. პარტნიორი უნივერსიტეტების ნომინირებული სტუდენტებისთვის უფასოა, დამოუკიდებელი აპლიკანტებისთვის — ზომიერი საფასური.
summary.ar: أكثر من 85 مقرراً بالإنجليزية بقيمة 5 أو 10 ساعات ECTS في جميع المجالات الأكاديمية في جامعة دنماركية ضمن أفضل 100 جامعة، مع برنامج اجتماعي حيوي. مجاني لطلاب الجامعات الشريكة المرشحين ورسوم معتدلة للمتقدمين المستقلين.

about.en:
AU Summer University brings about 2,500 students from 60+ countries to Aarhus, Denmark's second city, each summer. In 2027 there are two three-week terms (5–23 July and 26 July – 13 August) with 85+ English-taught courses from business and social sciences to nanoscience and biotechnology, taught by active researchers and worth 5 or 10 ECTS for transfer to your home university. Each term includes 15+ social events such as canoe trips, beach bonfires and a visit to the ARoS art museum.

Students from AU's international partner universities who are nominated by their home university pay no course fee; others apply as freemovers and pay a per-course fee in euros that depends on EU/non-EU citizenship, subject and credits (shown on each course page). Applications run 15 January – 10 March 2027.

en: 85+ English-taught courses, 5 or 10 ECTS
No course fee for nominated partner-university students
Strong social programme in Denmark's top student city

eligibility.en: Bachelor's and master's students (master's courses require a bachelor's degree); freemovers must meet English requirements. All nationalities; partner-university students can be nominated as exchange students.

en: Sign up for the 2027 course list and choose a course
Check with your international office whether you can be nominated (partner universities)
Otherwise apply as a freemover between 15 January and 10 March 2027 with passport, transcript and English proof
Pay the course fee (freemovers) and book housing; request a visa invitation if needed

costs.en: Partner-university nominees: no course fee. Freemovers: course fee in EUR per course (varies by EU/non-EU status, subject and ECTS; see course pages). AU's budget example per month: housing about EUR 570, meals EUR 240, social programme EUR 120.

score_reason: Large, credit-bearing Nordic summer university with 2027 dates and application window set.

org: KU Leuven (Faculties of Economics & Business, Arts and Social Sciences)

name.en: KU Leuven Europe Inside Out Summer School 2027
name.ka: KU Leuven-ის საზაფხულო სკოლა Europe Inside Out 2027
name.ar: المدرسة الصيفية Europe Inside Out في جامعة لوفان الكاثوليكية 2027

duration.ka: 2 ან 3 კვირა (2027 წლის 21 ივნისი – 2 ან 9 ივლისი)
duration.ar: أسبوعان أو ثلاثة (21 يونيو – 2 أو 9 يوليو 2027)

deadline_note: KU Leuven: registrations are open; they close 1 April 2027 (midnight CET) for non-European students and 1 May 2027 for European students.

summary.en: A two- or three-week course on doing business with Europe, EU policies and politics, entrepreneurship and culture at Belgium's top university, with trips to Brussels, Antwerp and Paris and 6–8 ECTS.
summary.ka: ორ- ან სამკვირიანი კურსი ევროპასთან ბიზნესის, ევროკავშირის პოლიტიკის, მეწარმეობისა და კულტურის შესახებ ბელგიის საუკეთესო უნივერსიტეტში, ექსკურსიებით ბრიუსელში, ანტვერპენსა და პარიზში და 6–8 ECTS კრედიტით.
summary.ar: مقرر لمدة أسبوعين أو ثلاثة عن الأعمال مع أوروبا وسياسات الاتحاد الأوروبي وريادة الأعمال والثقافة في أفضل جامعة بلجيكية، مع رحلات إلى بروكسل وأنتويرب وباريس و6–8 ساعات ECTS.

about.en:
Europe Inside Out is KU Leuven's EU-focused summer school, run jointly by its Faculties of Economics & Business, Arts and Social Sciences. Starting 21 June 2027, students study for two weeks (to 2 July, 6 ECTS) or three weeks (to 9 July, 8 ECTS), with lectures on Doing Business with Europe(ans), Policies & Politics in the EU, Entrepreneurship and Innovation in Europe and Social & Cultural Interactions, a group project presented on the final day, and day trips to Brussels, Antwerp and Paris included in the fee.

It targets graduate students in arts, economics and business, law or social sciences, and final-year undergraduates; participants must be over 18 with at least two years of higher education. Non-European students must register by 1 April 2027.

en: EU business, policy and culture at Belgium's oldest university
Day trips to Brussels, Antwerp and Paris included
6 or 8 ECTS with a group project

eligibility.en: Over 18 with at least two years in higher education: graduate students in arts, economics/business, law or social sciences, or final-year undergraduates (others need some exposure to these fields). All nationalities.

en: Read the 2027 flyer and provisional programme
Register online and select the applicable fee (partner or non-partner institution)
Pay within 14 days of registering
Non-European students: register by 1 April 2027 and arrange a Schengen visa and accommodation

costs.en: Registration fee (2027 page): two weeks EUR 600 (partner institutions) or EUR 1,000 (others); three weeks EUR 750 or EUR 1,150. Includes the programme and day trips; travel and accommodation not included.

score_reason: Affordable EU-themed credit summer school at a top European university; open now.

org: RWTH International Academy (RWTH Aachen University)

name.ar: المدارس الصيفية الهندسية في جامعة RWTH آخن 2027

deadline_note: RWTH International Academy: early-bird application deadline 20 February 2027 (pay by 1 March for 10% off); Country Scholarship applications by 1 April 2027. Final regular deadlines are given in each course's info package.

summary.en: Two-week, 3-ECTS engineering summer schools at one of Germany's top technical universities, on AI in industry, robotics (ROS), sustainable buildings, automotive tech and more, with housing, catering and transport included.
summary.ka: ორკვირიანი, 3-ECTS-იანი საინჟინრო საზაფხულო სკოლები გერმანიის ერთ-ერთ საუკეთესო ტექნიკურ უნივერსიტეტში: ხელოვნური ინტელექტი მრეწველობაში, რობოტიკა (ROS), მდგრადი შენობები, საავტომობილო ტექნოლოგიები და სხვა; საცხოვრებელი, კვება და ტრანსპორტი შედის.
summary.ar: مدارس صيفية هندسية لمدة أسبوعين (3 ساعات ECTS) في إحدى أفضل الجامعات التقنية الألمانية، في الذكاء الاصطناعي الصناعي والروبوتات (ROS) والمباني المستدامة وتقنيات السيارات وغيرها، مع السكن والوجبات والمواصلات.

about.en:
RWTH International Academy runs a series of two-week summer schools on the RWTH Aachen campus for international engineering and science students. 2027 courses include Artificial Intelligence in Industrial Applications (20 June – 3 July), Robot Operating Systems Essentials (20 June – 3 July, robot included), Sustainable Buildings & Green Cities (4–17 July), Automation and Simulation, Innovative Technologies in Automotive Engineering, Production Technology meets Industry 4.0, and Robotics and Innovation for Future Industries. Each two-week course gives 3 ECTS (about 75 hours of study).

Fees (EUR 2,490–2,990 for two weeks) include accommodation, catering and a transport ticket. There is a 10% early-bird discount (apply by 20 February, pay by 1 March 2027) and 50% Country Scholarships for students enrolled in listed countries (2027 list includes Türkiye, Egypt, South Korea, Malaysia, Indonesia, Brazil, Mexico and others, but not Georgia or Qatar), with a 1 April 2027 deadline.

en: Hands-on engineering topics: AI, robotics, sustainable cities, automotive
Accommodation, catering and transport included in the fee
Early-bird discount and 50% country scholarships

eligibility.en: University students in engineering, science or related fields (see each course's requirements); good English. Country Scholarships only for students enrolled at universities in the listed countries (Georgia and Qatar not listed for 2027).

en: Choose a 2027 summer school on the RWTH International Academy site and download its info package
Apply online (by 20 February 2027 for the early-bird discount)
If eligible, apply for the Country Scholarship by 1 April 2027
Pay the fee and arrange a visa if needed

costs.en: EUR 2,490 (most courses) to EUR 2,990 (ROS, robot included) for two weeks, including accommodation, catering and transport ticket; 10% early-bird discount; 50% Country Scholarship (e.g. EUR 1,245–1,495) for eligible countries.

score_reason: Practical engineering summer schools at a top technical university; all-inclusive but pricey.

org: Centre for Slovene as a Second and Foreign Language, Faculty of Arts, University of Ljubljana

name.ar: المدرسة الشتوية للغة السلوفينية 2027 (ليوبليانا)

deadline_note: Centre for Slovene: apply by completing the application form at least two weeks before the course begins (course starts 25 January 2027), so by about 11 January 2027. Diaspora scholarships for 2027 courses closed on 31 August 2026.

summary.en: A two-week intensive Slovene course in Ljubljana with an accompanying programme of lectures, workshops, cultural events and sport. Open to anyone wanting to learn Slovene; apply by early January 2027.
summary.ka: ორკვირიანი ინტენსიური სლოვენური ენის კურსი ლიუბლიანაში თანმხლები პროგრამით: ლექციები, ვორქშოფები, კულტურული ღონისძიებები და სპორტი. ღიაა ყველასთვის, ვისაც სლოვენურის სწავლა სურს; განაცხადი 2027 წლის იანვრის დასაწყისამდე.
summary.ar: دورة مكثفة في اللغة السلوفينية لمدة أسبوعين في ليوبليانا مع برنامج مصاحب من المحاضرات وورش العمل والفعاليات الثقافية والرياضة. مفتوحة لكل من يرغب في تعلم السلوفينية؛ التقديم حتى أوائل يناير 2027.

about.en:
The Winter School of Slovene Language is an intensive two-week course run by the University of Ljubljana's Centre for Slovene as a Second and Foreign Language, from 25 January to 5 February 2027. Participants follow a morning language course at their level (optional afternoon elective) and an accompanying programme of about 10 hours with lectures, workshops (for example a Kurent carnival-mask workshop), cultural events and sport, such as a guided visit to the National Museum of Contemporary History.

It suits anyone who wants to start or improve Slovene quickly, from complete beginners to advanced learners. Applications are made with the online form at least two weeks before the start.

en: Intensive Slovene at all levels in two weeks
Cultural accompanying programme in Ljubljana
Low fee compared with most European winter schools

eligibility.en: Adults of any nationality who want to learn Slovene; all levels.

en: Fill in the Winter School application form on centerslo.si
Apply at least two weeks before 25 January 2027
Pay the tuition as instructed
Arrange travel and accommodation in Ljubljana

costs.en: EUR 620 for the morning course and accompanying programme; EUR 240 for the optional afternoon elective. Accommodation and travel extra.

score_reason: Open, inexpensive language winter school; niche appeal.

org: University of Amsterdam (UvA Summer and Winter School)

name.en: University of Amsterdam Online Winter Courses 2027
name.ar: الدورات الشتوية عبر الإنترنت في جامعة أمستردام 2027

deadline_note: UvA course pages: early-bird deadline 1 November 2026 (EUR 50 off), regular admission deadline 13 December 2026 for the two-week courses running 18–29 January 2027.

summary.en: Short online winter courses from the University of Amsterdam on topics such as AI ethics and decision-making, existential psychology, Western esotericism and birding, with small partial scholarships for network universities.
summary.ka: მოკლე ონლაინ ზამთრის კურსები ამსტერდამის უნივერსიტეტიდან ისეთ თემებზე, როგორიცაა ხელოვნური ინტელექტის ეთიკა და გადაწყვეტილებების მიღება, ეგზისტენციალური ფსიქოლოგია, დასავლური ეზოთერიზმი და ფრინველებზე დაკვირვება, ქსელის უნივერსიტეტებისთვის მცირე ნაწილობრივი სტიპენდიებით.
summary.ar: دورات شتوية قصيرة عبر الإنترنت من جامعة أمستردام في موضوعات مثل أخلاقيات الذكاء الاصطناعي واتخاذ القرار وعلم النفس الوجودي والباطنية الغربية ومراقبة الطيور، مع منح جزئية صغيرة لطلاب جامعات الشبكات الشريكة.

about.en:
Every January the University of Amsterdam offers short online winter courses taught in English by UvA academics, open to students and professionals worldwide. For January 2027 the courses include Introduction to AI Ethics and Decision-Making and Existential Psychology for Contemporary Life (both online, 18–29 January 2027), Introduction to Western Esotericism, and a three-week online course, Birding Across Borders.

Courses are intensive and some include a preparatory assignment. Students from UNICA, Universitas 21 or LERU universities can request a EUR 100 partial scholarship on eligible courses (first-come, first-served), and UvA summer/winter alumni get EUR 75 off.

en: Learn from UvA academics without travelling
Two-week intensive online format in January
Small partial scholarships for network universities

eligibility.en: Mostly university students and professionals; each course states its own entry requirements. All nationalities; online.

en: Choose a 2027 winter course on the UvA Summer School site
Apply online with a motivation letter by 13 December 2026
Indicate an eligible scholarship or alumni discount in the form if applicable
Pay the tuition after admission and complete any preparatory assignment

costs.en: Two-week online courses: EUR 925 regular tuition (EUR 875 early bird, passed). Scholarships: UNICA/U21/LERU partial EUR 100; alumni discount EUR 75.

score_reason: Accessible online taster of a top European university; open until 13 December.

org: Fudan University (International Summer Session office)

name.ar: الدورة الصيفية الدولية في جامعة فودان (FISS) 2027

deadline_note: The 2026 session ran 13 July – 7 August 2026; the 2027 dates and deadlines are not yet published on the FISS site (it currently shows the winter session). Watch iss.fudan.edu.cn from early 2027.

summary.en: A four-week English-taught summer programme at Fudan in Shanghai with courses in business, history, science, society, medicine and law, Chinese language, kung fu and cultural trips; 7,000+ alumni since 2012.
summary.ka: ოთხკვირიანი ინგლისურენოვანი საზაფხულო პროგრამა ფუდანში, შანხაიში: კურსები ბიზნესში, ისტორიაში, მეცნიერებაში, საზოგადოებაში, მედიცინასა და სამართალში, ჩინური ენა, კუნგ-ფუ და კულტურული ექსკურსიები; 2012 წლიდან 7000-ზე მეტი კურსდამთავრებული.
summary.ar: برنامج صيفي لمدة أربعة أسابيع بالإنجليزية في جامعة فودان بشنغهاي يشمل مقررات في الأعمال والتاريخ والعلوم والمجتمع والطب والقانون، واللغة الصينية والكونغ فو ورحلات ثقافية؛ أكثر من 7000 خريج منذ 2012.

about.en:
Fudan International Summer Session (FISS) is a four-week English-taught programme for college students from around the world, held since 2012 with more than 7,000 participants. Content courses cover business and economy, history and culture, science and technology, society and politics, medicine and law; students can also take Chinese language at several levels and PE courses such as Chinese kung fu and folk dance, and study alongside Fudan degree students.

Activities include a campus tour, Shanghai city exploration, a Huangpu River cruise, company visits, dragon and lion dance and calligraphy. Participants receive a programme certificate and an official Fudan transcript. In 2026 tuition was a flat CNY 22,000 for up to 6 credits plus PE and Chinese, and Fudan offered no scholarships.

en: Up to 6 Fudan credits plus Chinese language
Courses across business, culture, science, politics, medicine and law
Shanghai cultural programme and company visits

eligibility.en: College/university students aged 18+ with sufficient English proficiency and in good health. All nationalities (UC students via UCEAP).

en: Watch iss.fudan.edu.cn for the 2027 session announcement
Apply on Fudan's online application system and pay the CNY 400 fee
After admission, pay tuition and enrol in courses
Arrange accommodation and a Chinese visa

costs.en: 2026: application fee CNY 400; tuition CNY 22,000 flat (CNY 19,800 for partner-nominated students; tuition waived for nominated exchange students). Accommodation, insurance and travel extra. No Fudan scholarships in 2026.

score_reason: Well-established Shanghai summer session; 2027 dates still to come.

org: Yonsei University (Winter Abroad at Yonsei, WAY)

name.ar: برنامج الشتاء في جامعة يونسي (WAY) 2026–2027

deadline_note: Yonsei WAY calendar: general application due 12 November 2026 (16:00 KST); tuition due 19 November 2026. Early-bird deadlines (October) have passed. Scholarship applications must be made within the application period.

summary.en: A three-week, credit-bearing English-taught winter programme on Yonsei's Sinchon campus in Seoul, for university students and admitted high-school seniors. Apply by 12 November 2026.
summary.ka: სამკვირიანი, კრედიტიანი ინგლისურენოვანი ზამთრის პროგრამა იონსეის სინჩონის კამპუსზე, სეულში, უნივერსიტეტის სტუდენტებისა და უნივერსიტეტში ჩარიცხული აბიტურიენტებისთვის. განაცხადის ვადა — 2026 წლის 12 ნოემბერი.
summary.ar: برنامج شتوي لمدة ثلاثة أسابيع بساعات معتمدة وباللغة الإنجليزية في حرم سينتشون لجامعة يونسي في سيول، لطلاب الجامعات وطلاب الثانوية المقبولين في جامعات. آخر موعد للتقديم 12 نوفمبر 2026.

about.en:
Winter Abroad at Yonsei (WAY) is a three-week, credit-bearing winter study-abroad programme taught in English at Yonsei University's Sinchon campus in central Seoul. Classes run 22 December 2026 – 8 January 2027, with optional orientation, campus dormitories (SK Global House, International House, Woo Jung Won) and a closing commencement ceremony; students can take one to three 3-credit courses.

It is open to undergraduate, master's and doctoral students at universities outside Korea and to high-school seniors with an official university admission letter, subject to a minimum GPA and a comprehensive review. The general application deadline is 12 November 2026, so apply quickly; small scholarships (for example a KRW 200,000 alumni scholarship) must be requested within the application period.

en: 3-credit English-taught courses over winter break in Seoul
Yonsei dormitories and Seoul in December–January
Open to university students and admitted high-school seniors

eligibility.en: Students currently studying at, or planning to attend, a college/university outside Korea (undergraduate, master's or doctoral), meeting the minimum cumulative GPA; high-school seniors need an official admission letter. All nationalities.

en: Apply online by 12 November 2026 (16:00 KST) with an official transcript, certificate of enrolment or admission letter and passport copy
Pay the KRW 100,000 application fee
Apply for any scholarship within the application period
Pay tuition by 19 November 2026 and register for courses (2nd registration 9–10 December)
Book a dormitory and arrange travel

costs.en: Application fee KRW 100,000. Tuition: KRW 1,870,000 (1 course), 3,070,000 (2) or 3,870,000 (3) at the general rate (lower early-bird rates have passed). Housing and travel extra.

score_reason: Open winter school at a top Korean university with a deadline in two weeks.

org: Weizmann Institute of Science (Weizmann School of Science)

name.ar: برنامج كوبتسينيت-غيتز الصيفي الدولي 2027 (معهد وايزمان)

deadline_note: Official 2027 timeline: online application opens 20 December 2026 and closes 20 January 2027; results in March 2027.

summary.en: An eight-week research summer at the Weizmann Institute for strong bachelor's and master's students in maths, computer science, physics, chemistry and life sciences. No fees, a USD 1,100 stipend, free housing and a flight subsidy.
summary.ka: რვაკვირიანი კვლევითი ზაფხული ვაიცმანის ინსტიტუტში ძლიერი ბაკალავრიატისა და მაგისტრატურის სტუდენტებისთვის მათემატიკაში, კომპიუტერულ მეცნიერებაში, ფიზიკაში, ქიმიასა და სიცოცხლის მეცნიერებებში. საფასური არ არის; სტიპენდია 1 100 აშშ დოლარი, უფასო საცხოვრებელი და ავიაბილეთის სუბსიდია.
summary.ar: صيف بحثي لثمانية أسابيع في معهد وايزمان لطلاب البكالوريوس والماجستير المتميزين في الرياضيات وعلوم الحاسوب والفيزياء والكيمياء وعلوم الحياة. بلا رسوم، مع منحة قدرها 1,100 دولار وسكن مجاني ودعم لتذكرة الطيران.

about.en:
The Kupcinet-Getz International Summer Program brings outstanding science students from around the world to the Weizmann Institute of Science in Rehovot, Israel, to work for eight weeks (16 June – 12 August 2027) as members of a research group. Each student is matched with a host lab in the faculties of Chemistry, Life Sciences, Mathematics and Computer Science, or Physics, based on up to five research topics chosen in the application. Weekends include organised trips around Israel.

There are no application, registration or tuition fees. Participants receive a USD 1,100 stipend, up to USD 400 towards flights, free accommodation for international students in dormitories near the campus, medical insurance and partial meal subsidies. Selection is by the Weizmann School of Science based on CV, transcript, motivation letter and recommendation letters.

en: Real lab research at one of the world's leading research institutes
No fees; USD 1,100 stipend, free housing and up to USD 400 flight subsidy
Matched to a host lab by your chosen research topics

eligibility.en: Bachelor's or master's students (not PhD) who have completed at least the first year of study, or recent bachelor's graduates planning further study, in physical sciences, chemistry, life sciences, mathematics or computer science. GPA of about 3.6/4.0 or equivalent and fluent English required. Open to students of all nationalities.

en: Prepare a CV with a passport-size photo, official transcript (with English translation if needed), passport title page and a one-page motivation letter
Apply online between 20 December 2026 and 20 January 2027 and choose up to five research topics
List at least one academic referee; they upload the letter through the link the system emails them
Results are announced in March 2027

costs.en: No application or tuition fees. Stipend USD 1,100 (two instalments), flight subsidy up to USD 400, free accommodation for international students, medical insurance and partial meal subsidies.

score_reason: Fully funded research summer at a top institute, open to all nationalities; 2027 dates published.

org: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI)

name.ar: زمالة WHOI الصيفية للطلاب 2027 (علوم المحيطات)

deadline_note: WHOI accepts applications each year from early December to early February; the deadline is 1 February (11:59 pm EST). 2027 dates follow this recurring pattern; decisions in mid-March.

summary.en: A paid 10–12-week ocean-science research fellowship for undergraduates finishing their third year. About 25–30 fellows; international students can apply and WHOI helps with the J-1 visa.
summary.ka: ანაზღაურებადი 10–12-კვირიანი კვლევითი სტიპენდია ოკეანის მეცნიერებებში მესამე კურსის დამამთავრებელი სტუდენტებისთვის. ყოველწლიურად 25–30 სტიპენდიანტი; საერთაშორისო სტუდენტებსაც შეუძლიათ განაცხადის შეტანა და WHOI J-1 ვიზაში ეხმარება.
summary.ar: زمالة بحثية مدفوعة لمدة 10–12 أسبوعاً في علوم المحيطات لطلاب البكالوريوس المنهين لسنتهم الثالثة. نحو 25–30 زميلاً سنوياً، ويمكن للطلاب الدوليين التقديم مع مساعدة المعهد في تأشيرة J-1.

about.en:
The Summer Student Fellowship (SSF) at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, on Cape Cod in Massachusetts, gives undergraduates a full summer of independent research in ocean science and engineering. Each fellow works on a project with a WHOI scientist or engineer, attends a lecture series introducing the many sides of marine science, and presents results at the end. Projects span biology, chemistry, geology, geophysics, physical oceanography, engineering, mathematics, meteorology and more.

The programme lasts 10–12 weeks. In 2026 the stipend was USD 721 per week plus a travel allowance of up to USD 720, and housing is arranged by WHOI. International students may apply: WHOI's foreign national adviser helps with the J-1 visa (proof of English proficiency required), and a 14% US federal tax is deducted from international fellows' stipends.

en: Independent research project with a WHOI scientist or engineer
Weekly stipend (USD 721/week in 2026) plus travel allowance
International students eligible; J-1 visa support

eligibility.en: Undergraduates who will have completed their junior (third) year by the start of the fellowship; students graduating before the fellowship starts are not eligible. Any science or engineering field. International students may apply (English proficiency proof needed for the visa).

en: Browse the potential projects list and identify possible advisers
Apply online between early December 2026 and 1 February 2027 (11:59 pm EST)
Submit short essays on research interests, a CV and unofficial transcripts
Arrange two references through the WHOI references system
Decisions are sent in mid-March

costs.en: No fees. Stipend of USD 721 per week (2026 rate) for 10–12 weeks, travel allowance up to USD 720, housing arranged. International fellows have 14% US federal tax deducted.

score_reason: Paid research fellowship at a world-leading ocean institute; internationals eligible with visa support.

org: Heidelberg Laureate Forum Foundation (HLFF)

name.ar: منتدى هايدلبرغ الرابع عشر للحائزين على الجوائز 2027 (الباحثون الشباب)

deadline_note: Official: application phase for the 14th HLF runs 11 November 2026 – 11 February 2027 (11:59 pm Berlin time). Decisions end of April 2027.

summary.en: A week in Heidelberg where 200 selected young mathematicians and computer scientists meet Abel, Turing, ACM Prize and Fields Medal laureates. Hotel and meals are covered; travel grants are available.
summary.ka: ერთი კვირა ჰაიდელბერგში, სადაც 200 შერჩეული ახალგაზრდა მათემატიკოსი და კომპიუტერული მეცნიერი ხვდება აბელის, ტიურინგის, ACM-ის პრემიისა და ფილდსის მედლის ლაურეატებს. სასტუმრო და კვება დაფარულია; ხელმისაწვდომია სამგზავრო გრანტები.
summary.ar: أسبوع في هايدلبرغ يلتقي فيه 200 باحث شاب مختار في الرياضيات وعلوم الحاسوب بالحائزين على جوائز آبل وتورينغ وجائزة ACM وميدالية فيلدز. الفندق والوجبات مغطاة، وتتوفر منح للسفر.

about.en:
The Heidelberg Laureate Forum (HLF) is an annual networking week in Heidelberg, Germany, where young researchers in mathematics and computer science spend time with laureates of the Abel Prize, ACM A.M. Turing Award, ACM Prize in Computing, Fields Medal, Nevanlinna/IMU Abacus Medal and other top awards. The 14th HLF runs 11–18 September 2027 with lectures, panels, workshops, a poster session and social events.

Undergraduate/pre-master's students, PhD students and postdocs (within five years of the PhD) can apply through a multi-step online application; reviewers are appointed by the award-granting institutions (ACM, the Norwegian Academy and IMU). The foundation books and pays for hotel accommodation and meals for the week; accepted researchers who cannot get travel funding at home can apply for an HLFF travel grant covering travel and visa costs.

en: Meet Abel, Turing and Fields laureates in small-group settings
Hotel accommodation and meals covered by the foundation
Travel grants available for those without other funding

eligibility.en: Students of mathematics, computer science or closely related fields at undergraduate/pre-master's level (enrolled, not yet holding a master's), PhD students, and postdocs within five years of the PhD (extended one year per child). Open to all nationalities.

en: Prepare a CV, motivational statement and transcripts (originals plus English translations)
Ask a professor or supervisor to submit a recommendation letter directly to the application system
Apply at application.heidelberg-laureate-forum.org between 11 November 2026 and 11 February 2027
If accepted (end of April), register and, if needed, apply for a travel grant between 3 May and 23 June 2027

costs.en: No fee. Hotel (single room, breakfast) 11–18 September 2027 and meals during the forum covered by HLFF. Travel is self-funded first; HLFF travel grants reimburse travel and visa costs if other funding is unavailable.

score_reason: Prestigious, largely funded forum with top laureates; application open from 11 Nov 2026.

org: CERN openlab

name.ar: برنامج CERN openlab الصيفي للطلاب 2027

deadline_note: CERN openlab says the 2027 call opens in November 2026; the closing date will be stated in the call (replies by late March/early April 2027). Exact deadline not yet published, so deadline left empty.

summary.en: A nine-week paid summer at CERN for bachelor's and master's students with strong computing skills, working on advanced IT projects with a CERN supervisor. All nationalities welcome.
summary.ka: ცხრაკვირიანი ანაზღაურებადი ზაფხული CERN-ში ბაკალავრიატისა და მაგისტრატურის სტუდენტებისთვის ძლიერი პროგრამირების უნარებით: თანამედროვე IT პროექტებზე მუშაობა CERN-ის ხელმძღვანელთან ერთად. ღიაა ყველა ეროვნების სტუდენტისთვის.
summary.ar: صيف مدفوع لتسعة أسابيع في سيرن لطلاب البكالوريوس والماجستير ذوي المهارات الحاسوبية القوية، للعمل على مشاريع تقنية متقدمة مع مشرف من سيرن. مفتوح لجميع الجنسيات.

about.en:
CERN openlab is CERN's public-private partnership for computing research. Each summer its Summer Student Programme brings bachelor's and master's students specialising in computer science and related fields to CERN near Geneva for nine weeks (starting 21 or 28 June 2027). Students work on projects in areas such as AI, quantum computing, data analytics and high-performance computing, each with a dedicated CERN supervisor, attend lectures by CERN experts and partner companies, and finish with a report and a short public presentation.

Participants receive an allowance of 94 CHF per calendar day, a lump-sum travel allowance, CERN health insurance and help finding accommodation. Candidates of all nationalities may apply. Decisions arrive by late March/early April 2027.

en: Nine weeks on computing projects at CERN with a dedicated supervisor
94 CHF per day allowance plus travel allowance and health insurance
Open to all nationalities

eligibility.en: Bachelor's or master's students (not PhD) in computer science, mathematics, engineering or physics with a strong computing profile, who will have completed at least 3 years (6 semesters) of full-time university study by summer 2027 and are still enrolled during the summer; good English; no previous CERN summer programme or more than 3 months at CERN.

en: Check the openlab page from November 2026 for the 2027 call
Prepare a CV, academic transcript and a motivation statement in English or French (PDF)
Click 'I am interested' on the call page and complete the application on CERN's recruitment system
Arrange reference letters as requested in the call
Replies by late March/early April 2027

costs.en: No fees. 94 CHF per calendar day allowance, lump-sum travel allowance, CERN health insurance; accommodation is paid by the student (CERN helps find it).

score_reason: Paid CERN computing internship open to all nationalities; 2027 call opens November 2026.

org: Fields Institute for Research in Mathematical Sciences

name.ar: برنامج فيلدز الصيفي للبحث لطلاب البكالوريوس (FUSRP) 2027

deadline_note: Fields plans to launch the FUSRP 2027 student application form on 2 November 2026; the deadline will be posted on the programme page. Deadline left empty until published.

summary.en: Two months of team research in mathematics for carefully selected undergraduates from around the world, at the Fields Institute in Toronto (with some projects at Western University).
summary.ka: ორთვიანი გუნდური კვლევა მათემატიკაში მსოფლიოს სხვადასხვა ქვეყნიდან შერჩეული ბაკალავრიატის სტუდენტებისთვის ტორონტოს Fields-ის ინსტიტუტში (ზოგი პროექტი დასავლეთ ონტარიოს უნივერსიტეტშია).
summary.ar: شهران من البحث الجماعي في الرياضيات لطلاب بكالوريوس مختارين من أنحاء العالم في معهد فيلدز بتورونتو (وبعض المشاريع في جامعة ويسترن).

about.en:
The Fields Undergraduate Summer Research Program (FUSRP) welcomes carefully selected undergraduates from around the world to the Fields Institute in Toronto for a research experience in the mathematical sciences from 1 June to 31 July 2027. Students work in small teams with a faculty supervisor on a defined project, with orientation, a graduate-school panel, a presentation clinic and final presentations on 30 July. In 2027 some project teams move to Western University in London, Ontario, from 8 June.

The programme is designed to lead to continued research and graduate study, and actively welcomes students from underrepresented groups. The student application form is planned to open on 2 November 2026 on the programme page, where the deadline and funding details will be posted.

en: Team research in pure and applied mathematics with a faculty supervisor
Hosted by a leading international mathematics institute
Open to undergraduates from around the world

eligibility.en: Undergraduate students in mathematics or related fields from any country (details and year-of-study requirements in the 2027 application form).

en: Check the FUSRP 2027 page from 2 November 2026 for the student application form
Prepare a CV, transcript and statement of research interests
Arrange reference letters as requested
Submit before the deadline posted on the page

costs.en: Check the 2027 call for stipend, travel and residence details (the programme includes residence check-in on 1 June). No application fee mentioned.

score_reason: International maths research summer at a top institute; 2027 applications open 2 Nov 2026.

org: Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics

name.en: Perimeter Institute Undergraduate Summer School & PSI Start Internship 2027
name.ka: პერიმეტრის ინსტიტუტის საზაფხულო სკოლა და PSI Start სტაჟირება 2027
name.ar: مدرسة معهد بيريميتر الصيفية وتدريب PSI Start للطلاب 2027

duration.en: 2-week school (14–25 June 2027); internship up to 15 weeks
duration.ar: مدرسة لأسبوعين (14–25 يونيو 2027)؛ تدريب حتى 15 أسبوعاً

deadline_note: Official 2027 dates: application opens mid-December 2026, deadline 17 January 2027, reference letters by 30 January 2027; selection by end of February 2027.

summary.en: A free two-week summer school in theoretical physics for about 30 undergraduates, plus paid research internships of up to 15 weeks. Students from anywhere in the world may apply; travel and housing are supported.
summary.ka: უფასო ორკვირიანი საზაფხულო სკოლა თეორიულ ფიზიკაში დაახლოებით 30 სტუდენტისთვის და ანაზღაურებადი კვლევითი სტაჟირება 15 კვირამდე. მონაწილეობა ნებისმიერი ქვეყნის სტუდენტს შეუძლია; მგზავრობა და საცხოვრებელი დაფინანსებულია.
summary.ar: مدرسة صيفية مجانية لأسبوعين في الفيزياء النظرية لنحو 30 طالباً جامعياً، إضافة إلى تدريبات بحثية مدفوعة حتى 15 أسبوعاً. يمكن للطلاب من أي بلد التقديم، مع دعم السفر والسكن.

about.en:
Perimeter Institute in Waterloo, Canada, the world's largest independent centre for theoretical physics, runs two linked undergraduate programmes. About 30 students attend a two-week Undergraduate Summer School (14–25 June 2027) with courses on modern theoretical physics, research talks and panels. Some are also selected for the PSI Start Research Internship, an in-person paid research placement of 12–15 weeks between 3 May and 13 August 2027 on projects in quantum gravity, quantum information, cosmology, mathematical physics and more.

There are no fees to apply or attend. Summer-school students receive travel support, accommodation and meal credit; interns are paid a research award plus round-trip airfare, housing help and meal credit. Students around the world who meet the criteria may apply; a visitor visa or eTA is normally needed.

en: Courses and talks at the world's largest independent theoretical physics centre
No fees; travel, housing and meals supported; interns are paid
Open to students worldwide

eligibility.en: Undergraduates who plan to apply to a graduate programme in physics starting in 2028 or later and who will have some knowledge of classical and quantum mechanics by June 2027; designed for students in their second-to-last undergraduate year. All nationalities welcome.

en: Sign up for an alert on the Perimeter page; the application opens in mid-December 2026
Prepare transcripts, a CV and a statement of interest (up to two pages)
Ask 2–3 referees to submit letters by 30 January 2027
Submit the online application by 17 January 2027 (you can apply to the school, the internship, or both)

costs.en: No application or programme fees. Summer school: travel support, accommodation and meal credit. Internship: paid research award, round-trip economy airfare, housing at a group rate and meal credit.

score_reason: Fully supported physics school and paid internship, open worldwide; 2027 deadline 17 Jan.

org: Max Planck Institute for Astronomy (MPIA)

name.en: MPIA Student Summer Internship 2027 (Max Planck Institute for Astronomy)
name.ka: MPIA-ს საზაფხულო სტაჟირება 2027 (მაქს პლანკის ასტრონომიის ინსტიტუტი)
name.ar: تدريب معهد ماكس بلانك لعلم الفلك الصيفي للطلاب 2027 (MPIA)

deadline_note: MPIA says the next call will be announced in December 2026 with applications due in January 2027. The 2026 deadline was 15 January; 2027 date estimated from that pattern.

summary.en: Fully funded summer research internships in astronomy and astrophysics in Heidelberg for bachelor's and master's students anywhere in the world, with salary, travel costs and at least two places for developing countries.
summary.ka: სრულად დაფინანსებული საზაფხულო კვლევითი სტაჟირება ასტრონომიასა და ასტროფიზიკაში ჰაიდელბერგში მსოფლიოს ნებისმიერი ქვეყნის ბაკალავრიატისა და მაგისტრატურის სტუდენტებისთვის: ხელფასი, მგზავრობის ხარჯები და მინიმუმ ორი ადგილი განვითარებადი ქვეყნებისთვის.
summary.ar: تدريبات بحثية صيفية ممولة بالكامل في علم الفلك والفيزياء الفلكية في هايدلبرغ لطلاب البكالوريوس والماجستير من أي مكان في العالم، مع راتب وتكاليف سفر ومقعدين على الأقل لطلاب الدول النامية.

about.en:
The Max Planck Institute for Astronomy in Heidelberg offers fully funded summer internships in which bachelor's and master's students join a research group and work on a defined project, from exoplanets and star formation to the Milky Way, galaxies and instrumentation. Applicants rank their top five projects from a published list. More than 1,000 applications were received for 2026, so selection is very competitive.

Interns receive a salary of about EUR 1,000 per month net with social benefits, travel costs are supported and the institute helps find accommodation. At least two internships are reserved for candidates from developing countries (per MPIA's attached list). The next call is announced in December 2026 with applications due in January 2027.

en: Hands-on research in a leading astronomy institute
About EUR 1,000/month net salary plus travel support
At least two places for students from developing countries

eligibility.en: Bachelor's and master's students anywhere in the world (not yet holding a master's degree). Bachelor's students must have completed at least four semesters by the start of the internship to qualify for a visa. AI-generated statements are discouraged.

en: Watch the MPIA internship page for the call in December 2026
Read the project list and choose your top five projects
Prepare a CV, a one-page research statement, transcripts and the MPIA transcript form
Submit through the online system by the January 2027 deadline (15 January in 2026)

costs.en: No fees. Salary of about EUR 1,000 per month net with social benefits; travel costs supported; help finding accommodation (rent paid by the intern).

score_reason: Funded astronomy internship open worldwide with places for developing countries; call due January.

org: Stanford Pre-Collegiate Studies, Stanford University

name.ar: معاهد ستانفورد الصيفية لما قبل الجامعة 2027 (عبر الإنترنت)

deadline_note: 2026 deadline was Friday 13 March (11:59 pm PT) with sessions 15–26 June and 6–17 July; 2027 deadline estimated from that pattern (one admissions round). Financial aid deadline is about one week later.

summary.en: Two-week online enrichment courses from Stanford Pre-Collegiate Studies in maths, science, humanities and business for students in grades 8–11 worldwide. Need-based aid is open to international students.
summary.ka: Stanford Pre-Collegiate Studies-ის ორკვირიანი ონლაინ კურსები მათემატიკაში, მეცნიერებაში, ჰუმანიტარულ საგნებსა და ბიზნესში მსოფლიოს 8–11 კლასის მოსწავლეებისთვის. საჭიროებაზე დაფუძნებული დახმარება საერთაშორისო მონაწილეებსაც ეხება.
summary.ar: دورات إثرائية عبر الإنترنت لمدة أسبوعين من ستانفورد لما قبل الجامعة في الرياضيات والعلوم والإنسانيات والأعمال لطلاب الصفوف 8–11 حول العالم، مع مساعدة مالية حسب الحاجة متاحة للطلاب الدوليين.

about.en:
Stanford Pre-Collegiate Summer Institutes is a selective, non-credit online enrichment programme run by Stanford Pre-Collegiate Studies. Students take one intensive two-week course taught live by Stanford-affiliated instructors, chosen from a catalogue covering mathematics (e.g. number theory, cryptography), science, computer science, humanities, social science and business. In 2026 there were two sessions: 15–26 June and 6–17 July.

The programme is open to students worldwide in grades 8–11 who are between 13 and 19 during the programme. Applicants rank up to three courses and submit transcripts and short responses; there is one admissions round, with decisions in mid-May.

en: Live online university-style courses from Stanford-affiliated instructors
Wide STEM catalogue: maths, CS, physics, biology and more
Need-based financial aid for domestic and international students

eligibility.en: Students currently in grades 8–11 (or equivalent) who will be older than 13 and younger than 19 during the programme; open to students from any country. Some courses have grade-level limits.

en: Browse the course catalogue when the 2027 courses are published (winter 2026/27)
Complete the online application and rank up to three courses
Upload unofficial transcripts for the past academic year and a half
Pay the USD 65 application fee (waivers available)
If needed, submit the financial aid application about one week after the admissions deadline

costs.en: Tuition USD 3,200 (2026) plus up to USD 100 for course materials; USD 65 application fee. Need-based financial aid for domestic and international students (USD 60 aid application fee, waivers possible).

score_reason: Accessible online Stanford enrichment open worldwide with aid; deadline estimated mid-March.

org: Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf (HZDR)

name.ar: برنامج HZDR الصيفي للطلاب 2027

deadline_note: Official 2027 dates: applications 2 November 2026 – 24 January 2027 (10 pm CET); notifications by end of March 2027; programme July–September 2027.

summary.en: Eight paid weeks in a Helmholtz research team in Dresden for senior bachelor's and master's students in natural sciences, life sciences, medicine and engineering from around the world. Salary, guesthouse housing and a travel allowance are provided.
summary.ka: რვა ანაზღაურებადი კვირა დრეზდენში ჰელმჰოლცის კვლევით ჯგუფში ბუნებისმეტყველების, სიცოცხლის მეცნიერებების, მედიცინისა და ინჟინერიის ბოლო კურსების ბაკალავრებისა და მაგისტრანტებისთვის მთელი მსოფლიოდან. ხელფასი, სტუმართა სახლში ცხოვრება და მგზავრობის კომპენსაცია.
summary.ar: ثمانية أسابيع مدفوعة ضمن فريق بحثي في مركز هيلمهولتز بدريسدن لطلاب البكالوريوس المتقدمين والماجستير في العلوم الطبيعية وعلوم الحياة والطب والهندسة من أنحاء العالم، مع راتب وسكن في دار الضيافة وبدل سفر.

about.en:
Every summer the Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf (HZDR), one of Germany's large national research centres, welcomes international students for eight weeks between July and September to work on a real project in one of its research teams, in areas such as materials research, energy, health (radiation and cancer research) and matter (accelerators, high magnetic fields, lasers). Each student has a supervisor who plans a project; participants also attend selected lectures and lab tours across HZDR and receive feedback at the end.

Students from around the world can apply between 2 November 2026 and 24 January 2027. HZDR pays a salary to cover daily expenses, provides housing in the student guesthouse and gives a travel allowance to Germany depending on place of residence (EU or non-EU).

en: Real project in a Helmholtz research team with a personal supervisor
Salary, guesthouse housing and travel allowance
Open to students from around the world

eligibility.en: Enrolled senior university students of natural sciences, life sciences, medicine, technology or related fields with very good English, who will have completed at least three years of university study by 30 September 2027 and remain enrolled (bachelor's or master's) after summer 2027. PhD students and anyone who has already had an HZDR contract or stipend are not eligible. All nationalities.

en: Fill in the online application form between 2 November 2026 and 24 January 2027
Upload transcripts and proof of enrolment (start date and enrolment until at least 30 September 2027) as one PDF
After pressing 'Finish', send the generated link to a professor or senior scientist for the recommendation letter
Notifications are emailed by end of March 2027

costs.en: No fees. HZDR pays a salary for daily expenses, provides housing in the student guesthouse and a travel allowance (amount depends on EU or non-EU residence). The application form asks you to confirm you cover remaining travel costs.

score_reason: Funded Helmholtz summer research open worldwide; 2027 application open 2 Nov 2026 – 24 Jan 2027.

summary.ka: ათკვირიანი პროგრამა იულიხის სუპერკომპიუტერებზე კვლევით პროექტებზე სამუშაოდ იმ სტუდენტებისთვის, ვინც პირველი ხარისხი დაასრულა, მაგრამ მაგისტრატურა ჯერ არ დაუმთავრებია (საბუნებისმეტყველო, საინჟინრო, კომპიუტერული მეცნიერება, მათემატიკა). ინგლისურ ენაზე, ხარჯების ანაზღაურებით.

about.en:
The Jülich Supercomputing Centre (JSC) at Forschungszentrum Jülich, one of Europe's largest research centres, has run a guest student programme every summer since 2000, supported by CECAM. Participants begin with an introductory course on parallel computing and the Jülich supercomputers, then join a local scientist to work on a current research topic, in fields such as mathematics, physics, chemistry, neuroscience, software tools, visualisation, distributed and quantum computing, and AI.

The programme lasts ten weeks between August and October (2026 edition: 3 August – 9 October) and is held in English. Students receive an expense allowance and must live in Jülich for the whole programme; Forschungszentrum Jülich helps find accommodation, but travel and accommodation are paid by the participant.

en: Hands-on research on some of Europe's most powerful supercomputers
Introductory course in parallel computing, then a supervised project
Expense allowance; held in English

eligibility.en: Students of natural sciences, engineering, computer science or mathematics who have completed their first degree (bachelor's) but not yet finished their master's, with experience in the computer-oriented parts of their subject. A recommendation letter from a university lecturer or professor is required. No nationality restriction is stated.

en: Check the JSC 'Apply for the next programme' page from the end of 2026
Prepare a CV, transcripts and a statement of interest in English or German
Ask a lecturer or professor for a recommendation letter
Submit the online application before the deadline (30 April in 2026)

costs.en: No fees. Participants receive an expense allowance but pay their own travel and accommodation (help finding housing is offered).

score_reason: Long-running HPC research summer with allowance; 2027 call opens end of 2026.

summary.ka: ასტრონავტის მომზადების კვირა ინგლისურ ენაზე ბელგიის კოსმოსურ ცენტრში 9–18 წლის ბავშვებისთვის: მრავალღერძიანი სავარძელი, სრული სიმულირებული კოსმოსური მისია და ვირტუალური გასეირნება მთვარეზე. პანსიონით ან დღის ფორმატით.
summary.ar: أسبوع من تدريب رواد الفضاء باللغة الإنجليزية في مركز الفضاء البلجيكي للأعمار 9–18: كرسي متعدد المحاور ومهمة فضائية محاكاة كاملة ومشي على القمر بالواقع الافتراضي، مع خيار الإقامة أو الحضور النهاري.

about.en:
The Euro Space Center in Transinne, in the Belgian Ardennes, runs residential space camps for young people. The English-language Astronaut Camp lasts six days and five nights: campers train on the multi-axis chair (disorientation training), fly a complete simulated space mission from lift-off and orbit to satellite deployment and landing, and try Moonwalk/Marswalk VR experiences of lunar and Martian gravity, alongside lessons on space science.

The 2027 English sessions are 19–23 July, 2–6 August and 30 August – 3 September. Campers can board (Sunday 5 pm to Friday 4 pm, meals and lodging included) or attend as day students. Booking is by an online pre-reservation that the team then confirms.

en: Astronaut training: multi-axis chair, mission simulation, VR moonwalk
Run in English for ages 9–18
Residential option with meals and lodging included

eligibility.en: Young people aged 9 to 18. The camp is taught in English; the booking form accepts participants from any country (check visa needs for Belgium/Schengen).

en: Choose a 2027 English session on the Euro Space Center camp page
Select boarding or day camp and submit the online pre-reservation
Wait for the team to confirm and send payment details
Questions: camps@eurospacecenter.be or +32 61 65 01 33 (weekdays 9:00–16:00)

costs.en: Paid camp; the price for boarding or day attendance is shown at booking (boarding includes meals, lodging, T-shirt and astronaut badge). Travel to Belgium not included.

score_reason: Fun hands-on space camp in English for younger students; 2027 sessions bookable.

summary.ar: دورات بحثية سكنية لمدة أربعة أسابيع لطلاب المدارس الثانوية: البحث في العلوم البيولوجية (RIBS) في مختبرات جامعة شيكاغو، أو العمل الميداني في علم الحفريات مع متحف فيلد. يمكن للطلاب الدوليين التقديم.

about.en:
The University of Chicago's Pre-College 'Practicum' track offers intensive, hands-on research courses. In Research in the Biological Sciences (RIBS), students learn advanced laboratory techniques used in molecular and cell biology and carry out experiments in UChicago lab facilities. In Stones and Bones, students spend four weeks with Field Museum palaeontologists in Chicago and on fieldwork in Wyoming, learning how fossils are collected, analysed and conserved.

Practicum courses are fully residential on the UChicago campus (no remote option) and are for current 10th and 11th graders aged at least 15. Practicum applicants must apply by the priority deadline (13 January 2027). International students are welcome but must check UChicago's visa requirements for their programme type.

en: Real lab techniques in a top research university (RIBS)
Palaeontology fieldwork in Wyoming with the Field Museum (Stones and Bones)
Need-based partial aid available, including for international families

eligibility.en: High-school students currently in 10th or 11th grade (or equivalent), at least 15 years old. International students may apply (visa requirements apply).

en: Use the Course Finder to choose RIBS or Stones and Bones
Complete the online application by 13 January 2027 (priority deadline required for Practicum)
Upload transcripts for grades 9–11 and a current grade report, and request a teacher/counsellor recommendation
Pay the USD 75 application fee (waived if you apply for financial aid)
Decisions are released in mid-March 2027

costs.en: Practicum programme fee USD 15,200 (2026 figure) including residence. Need-based partial aid (for household income ≤ USD 125,000 the 4-week practicum cost was USD 7,600; ≤ USD 80,000 USD 3,800). USD 75 application fee. Travel and visa costs extra.

score_reason: Real lab or field research for high-schoolers at a top university; 2027 priority deadline 13 Jan.

summary.ar: دورات ما قبل الجامعة في جامعة شيكاغو حضورياً أو عبر الإنترنت، من الإثراء لمدة أسبوعين إلى دورات Immersion بمستوى جامعي في العلوم والرياضيات والاقتصاد وغيرها. يُرحَّب بالطلاب الدوليين.

about.en:
University of Chicago Summer Session offers high-school students several pre-college formats: residential Enrichment (short academic experiences), Career Insight (faculty- and industry-led courses), Immersion (undergraduate-level courses taught by UChicago faculty with projects and field trips), the research Practicum, and remote options such as 3–5-week Summer Online courses taken alongside UChicago undergraduates.

Applications for summer 2027 have two deadlines: priority on 13 January 2027 and regular on 3 March 2027. The application asks for transcripts, a recommendation and short responses; some STEM courses ask for test scores. International students may apply and should check UChicago's visa guidance for residential programmes.

en: Wide choice of residential and online courses, including STEM and economics
Immersion courses are taught at undergraduate level by UChicago faculty
Need-based partial aid for domestic and international families

eligibility.en: High-school students (typically grades 9–11 depending on programme; Practicum is 10th–11th grade). International students welcome, subject to visa requirements.

en: Use the Course Finder to choose a programme and course
Apply online by 13 January 2027 (priority) or 3 March 2027 (regular)
Upload transcripts and a 2026–27 grade report; request a recommendation
Pay the USD 75 application fee (waived if applying for aid)
Apply for aid by the priority deadline; awards are limited

costs.en: 2026 fees: Enrichment USD 3,000; Career Insight USD 5,890; Immersion USD 9,300; Practicum USD 15,200; Summer Online USD 4,980. Need-based partial aid available. USD 75 application fee. Travel and visa costs extra.

score_reason: Selective pre-college summer at a top university; 2027 deadlines published.

summary.ka: შვიდკვირიანი კვლევითი პროგრამა მასალათმცოდნეობაში სტონი ბრუკის ლაბორატორიებში, სადაც სკოლის მოსწავლეები რეალურ პოლიმერულ და ნანომასალების პროექტებზე მუშაობენ და Materials Research Society-ის კონფერენციაზე წარდგენას ისახავენ მიზნად.
summary.ar: برنامج بحثي لسبعة أسابيع في علوم المواد بمختبرات ستوني بروك، يعمل فيه طلاب الثانوية على مشاريع حقيقية في البوليمرات والمواد النانوية ويهدفون إلى عرضها في مؤتمر جمعية أبحاث المواد.

about.en:
The Garcia Research Scholars Program at Stony Brook University (New York) is an interdisciplinary summer research programme that pairs high-school students with faculty, graduate students and undergraduates on projects in materials science, polymers, medicine, energy and computation. A goal of the summer is to take projects far enough for students to submit abstracts to the Materials Research Society (MRS) Fall Meeting, where accepted work is presented.

The 2026 programme ran 24 June – 7 August. International students are welcome, but the Garcia programme cannot sponsor visas: applicants must already have documents allowing them to be legally present in the US for the programme period. The programme also accepts undergraduates and teachers.

en: Real lab research with possible presentation at the MRS Fall Meeting
Interdisciplinary materials, polymer and nanotech projects
International students accepted if they can be legally present in the US

eligibility.en: High-school students at least 16 years old by early July of the programme year, with an unweighted GPA of about 95/100 (3.8/4.0) and strong science/maths coursework. International students may apply but the programme cannot support visa applications.

en: Check the Garcia Apply page in winter 2026/27 for the 2027 application
Complete Part 1 and Part 2 of the online application
Have your school send transcripts and three recommendation letters (one from a science teacher) directly
Pay the non-refundable USD 50 registration fee
Decisions are usually released in early April

costs.en: 2026: laboratory usage fee USD 4,000 (not including room or board); optional campus room about USD 2,599 for the programme; mandatory health services fee USD 66; optional meal plan. No financial aid or scholarships offered.

score_reason: Real materials research for high-schoolers; no visa support and 2027 deadline not yet posted.

about.en:
The Aalto University Science Institute (AScI) International Summer Research Programme hires 50+ research-driven students each summer to work as research assistants in groups across Aalto's School of Science and its three Schools of Engineering in Espoo, near Helsinki. Projects range from physics, mathematics and computer science to materials, energy and neuroscience; students apply to one to three projects from a list published in mid-December. In 2026 there were 5,500 applications from 133 countries and 70 interns from 28 countries.

The internship lasts 12 weeks in June–August (flexible by group) and includes a 'get to know Finland' course and a poster exhibition. Interns are employed by the research group with a salary of 2,000+ EUR per month depending on years of study, a travel bonus of 400 EUR (from inside Europe) or 800 EUR (from outside Europe), paid time off and help finding low-cost student housing.

en: Salaried research job in a top Nordic university (2,000+ EUR/month)
Travel bonus up to 800 EUR for students from outside Europe
Open worldwide; choose up to three projects

summary.ar: النسخة الإيطالية من برنامج PROMYS: ستة أسابيع في نظرية الأعداد للموهوبين رياضياً بين 15 و18 عاماً في جامعة بادوفا، بالإنجليزية. التكاليف مدعومة بشكل كبير، ويمكن للمساعدة حسب الحاجة أن تغطي كل شيء.

about.en:
PROMYS Italia, launched in 2025 by the University of Padova's mathematics department with the PROMYS Foundation, follows the Boston PROMYS model: first-year students explore number theory through daily problem sets, lectures and discussions with undergraduate counsellors, guided by the principles of exploration and discovery. Courses are taught in English; the rest of the programme runs in English and Italian. In 2026 it ran 12 July – 22 August in Padova, with places for returning students on more advanced courses.

Applicants must solve a challenging problem set (sent when applications open in January to those who register interest by email) and submit it with a recommendation letter, high-school transcript and an application form with short answers. The 2026 deadline was 5 March, with decisions by 30 April.

en: PROMYS-style number theory immersion in a historic university city
Courses taught in English
Real cost of 6,000 EUR subsidised to 3,500 EUR; need-based aid up to full cost

eligibility.en: Students who by the first day of the programme have completed at least 9th grade (or equivalent), are at least 15 years old, and are not yet full-time university students (the summer before university or a gap year is fine). No nationality restriction is stated.

en: Email promys@math.unipd.it to register interest
When applications open (5 January in 2026) you receive the problem set
Write up your solutions and complete the application form with short answers
Send a recommendation letter and your high-school transcript
Submit before the deadline (5 March in 2026); decisions by end of April

costs.en: Cost in 2026: 3,500 EUR for the six-week residential programme (the real cost of 6,000 EUR is subsidised for every student). Generous need-based financial aid up to the full cost of participation.

score_reason: New European PROMYS edition with heavy subsidies and aid; dates estimated from 2026.

The Honors Summer Math Camp (HSMC), run by Mathworks at Texas State University in San Marcos, is a full-time, in-person six-week camp for mathematically talented high-school students. First-year campers take an intensive course in number theory and proof-based problem solving alongside other classes and seminars; second- and third-year students work with research mentors on original projects, many of which have won awards in national science competitions.

The 2027 camp runs 20 June – 31 July. Admission is rolling from 1 December until the camp is full, with first acceptances on 15 February. Most campers come from across the US, but students from countries including Albania, Hungary, Bulgaria, Spain, South Korea, Taiwan, China, Indonesia, Mexico and England have attended.

The Oxford Machine Learning School (OxML), organised by AI for Global Goals, has trained more than 8,000 learners from 142 countries since 2019. OxML 2027 has three programmes: Foundation Models (June 2027, online only) on how large models are built, trained, evaluated and applied; Biomedical AI (10–12 August 2027) on clinical data, genomics, proteins and molecular design; and Frontier AI (13–15 August 2027). The August programmes can be attended in Oxford with online access, or fully online.

Registration is open now: participants choose individual programmes or a Comprehensive pass for all three, and full-time students can register at a student rate with an academic reference. Lectures are given by researchers from universities and industry labs.

en: Lectures by leading ML researchers on foundation models and biomedical AI
Attend in Oxford or online
Student rate with an academic reference

eligibility.en: Open to students (undergraduate, master's, PhD), researchers and professionals worldwide with a quantitative or technical background. Student prices require a current academic reference. In-person attendees arrange their own UK visa if needed.

Open the registration page and choose Standard or Student registration
Select the Comprehensive pass or individual programmes and online or Oxford format
Enter your details (and academic reference for the student rate) and pay securely online

about.en:
Neuromatch Academy is a global, non-profit online summer school. Its courses are full-time, synchronous programmes held every July: Computational Neuroscience and Deep Learning (5–23 July 2027), and NeuroAI and Computational Behaviour (12–23 July 2027). Participants are matched into pods of 10–15 students with a dedicated teaching assistant by time slot, research interests and language, and spend about 4.5 hours a day on interactive tutorials (Python notebooks) and 3 hours on a group research project with a project TA and mentor.

Courses run in five time slots around the world so students can attend in their daytime, and tuition is globally adjusted to keep the programme accessible. Participants must attend live (no more than two absences for a certificate). Applications for the July 2027 Academy open on 10 February 2027 via the Neuromatch portal.

en: Live, pod-based learning with teaching assistants and a real group project
Courses in computational neuroscience, deep learning and NeuroAI
Five time-zone slots and country-adjusted tuition

eligibility.en: Open worldwide to undergraduate and graduate students, researchers and professionals who meet each course's prerequisites (Python, linear algebra and calculus; NeuroAI requires CompNeuro and Deep Learning or equivalent). Must be able to commit about 8 hours a day for the course weeks.

en: Check the prerequisites for your chosen course on the Neuromatch courses page
Create an account on the Neuromatch Academy portal
Apply from 10 February 2027, choosing your course and a daytime time-zone slot
If accepted, pay the country-adjusted tuition (or request any available support) and complete pre-course preparation

costs.en: Tuition is globally adjusted by country of residence (amounts shown in the application portal). Online, so no travel or housing costs.

score_reason: Highly regarded, accessible online research-oriented school with country-adjusted fees.

The Mediterranean Machine Learning (M2L) Summer School offers a focused five-day programme of keynotes, lectures and practical sessions led by experienced AI researchers from around the world, covering computer vision, natural language processing, generative and diffusion models, reinforcement learning, applied deep learning, neuroscience and ethics. Participants can present their research in poster sessions for early feedback, and social and cultural activities support networking. The 2027 edition takes place in Barcelona, Spain, from 30 August to 3 September.

The school is advertised with a public call and participants are selected on merit. The main audience is doctoral students and exceptional master's students, plus academics and practitioners, from all over the world with a focus on the Mediterranean area. M2L actively promotes diversity through scholarships and outreach.

en: Lectures and labs from leading AI researchers
Poster session to present your own research
Scholarships to support diversity

eligibility.en: Primarily PhD students and exceptional master's students in machine learning or related fields, plus academics and practitioners, from anywhere in the world (focus on the Mediterranean region).

Prepare a CV and a short description of your research or ML experience as requested in the call
Apply online and indicate if you need a scholarship
If selected, register and arrange travel to Barcelona

costs.en: Registration fee and scholarship details are published with the call. Scholarships are offered to promote diversity; travel and accommodation are usually the participant's responsibility unless covered by a scholarship.

about.en:
The UCSC Scholar Immersion Program (SIP), formerly the Science Internship Program, places high-school students in research projects mentored by University of California, Santa Cruz researchers across the sciences, engineering and other divisions. SIP 2027 is in person, with an online research week (14–17 June), move-in on 20 June and in-person research weeks from 21 June to 6 August, ending in a presentation day. On-campus housing is offered.

Applicants choose from the 2027 research project list and submit transcripts, GPA and one academic reference. Admission decisions are independent of financial need; qualifying scholars receive aid packages covering 25–100% of tuition and programme fees. SIP warns that no third-party agency may charge extra fees: apply only through the official portal.

On-campus housing and a final presentation day
Need-based aid covering 25–100% of costs

Apply on the SIP portal between 15 January and 26 February 2027 (noon PST)
Upload unofficial transcripts and GPA; your academic reference is due 5 March 2027
Pay the USD 68 application fee (waivers on request) and optionally submit financial documents
Offers roll out from 9 April 2027; a deposit secures your place

about.en:
The Santa Fe Institute (SFI) in New Mexico is a world-leading centre for complexity science. Its Undergraduate Complexity Research (UCR) programme brings undergraduates from the physical, natural and social sciences and mathematics to SFI for ten weeks (30 May – 7 August 2027) to carry out an independent research project with an SFI mentor, alongside lectures, workshops and the institute's interdisciplinary community. It is a full-time, in-person programme.

Participants receive a USD 7,000 stipend, free housing and meals during the residential stay, and travel support to and from Santa Fe. International students are welcome: those at US institutions usually join on F-1 CPT, and those enrolled outside the US are also eligible, with SFI possibly sponsoring a J-1 visa. Strong quantitative or programming skills are favoured; priority usually goes to students entering their junior or senior year.

USD 7,000 stipend plus free housing, meals and travel support
Open to international undergraduates, including those studying outside the US (J-1 support possible)

Upload a current academic CV and unofficial transcripts (with English cover translation if needed)
Answer two research-statement prompts, including a short project proposal

costs.en: No fees. USD 7,000 stipend, free housing and meals during the residential programme, and travel support to and from Santa Fe.

about.en:
The Pembroke Cambridge Summer Programme is run by Pembroke College itself, one of the oldest colleges of the University of Cambridge. From 10 July to 21 August 2027 students live in the college and take three courses across two modules, taught in small lectures and seminars by Cambridge-affiliated academics. The 2027 portfolio covers economics, politics and international relations, history, literature, film, neuroscience, public health, cyber security, materials science and more; students planning research can replace one course with an Independent Supervision Research Project with one-to-one supervision.

It is open to university students worldwide who will have completed at least their first year of university by July 2027, with a GPA of at least 3.2/4.0 (3.5 recommended) or equivalent and a high level of English. Applications are rolling, so earlier applicants get the cheaper rooms. An official transcript is issued for credit transfer. Pembroke does not offer general financial aid (its small 1976 Scholarships are only for University of California students).

en: Run by Pembroke College, University of Cambridge
Small-group teaching, three courses or a one-to-one research project
Six weeks living and dining in a historic Cambridge college

org: University of Oxford, Department for Continuing Education

name.en: Oxford University Summer School for Adults (OUSSA) 2027
name.ar: المدرسة الصيفية للبالغين بجامعة أكسفورد (OUSSA) 2027

summary.ar: أكثر من 60 دورة معتمدة مدة كل منها أسبوع في Rewley House بأكسفورد لكل من بلغ 18 عامًا، في الأدب والتاريخ والفن والفلسفة والآثار والعلوم وغيرها، بحلقات نقاش لا تتجاوز 12 طالبًا ودروس فردية.

about.en:
The Oxford University Summer School for Adults (OUSSA) is run by the University of Oxford's Department for Continuing Education at Rewley House in central Oxford. In 2027 it runs in six one-week blocks from 3 July to 14 August; participants pick one or more week-long courses from a list of 60+ in literature, creative writing, history, archaeology, architecture, history of art, philosophy, theology, psychology and biological sciences. Each week has morning seminars of no more than 12 students, two one-to-one tutorials, guest lectures, access to the Bodleian library and a social programme.

It is open to anyone aged 18 or over (students, graduates and lifelong learners) of any nationality. Each course carries 10 CATS credits at undergraduate level (FHEQ Level 4) for students who attend all classes and complete a 1,000-word assignment or presentation; a 1,500-word pre-course assignment is compulsory. Non-native speakers need strong English (IELTS 7.5 with 7.0 in each part, or equivalent, unless waived).
