about.en:
The Centro de Lenguas Modernas (CLM) is the University of Granada's own language centre, accredited by the Instituto Cervantes. Its 'Curso de verano de Lengua y Cultura' runs in two monthly sessions in 2027, 2–29 June and 2–29 July (or both, 180 hours). Each month students build a 90-hour timetable from Spanish language classes and 22.5- or 45-hour subjects such as Spanish and Latin American literature, history of Spain and its art, Islamic culture in Spain, Spanish business law, international marketing, renewable energy and sustainability in the Mediterranean; a few June subjects are taught in English, and internships (volunteering, law, business, healthcare) can be added.

The course is for intermediate and advanced learners (B1.1 to C2) and suits university students who want transferable credit and a summer in Granada, home of the Alhambra. The CLM also offers accommodation help, cultural and sports activities and a language exchange.

summary.en: A one-week winter school in Antwerp on crisis leadership, communication and resilience, with case studies and speakers from the fire service, Brussels Airport and the Port of Antwerp-Bruges; 3 ECTS.
summary.ka: ერთკვირიანი ზამთრის სკოლა ანტვერპენში კრიზისულ ლიდერობაზე, კომუნიკაციასა და მდგრადობაზე — ქეისებითა და მომხსენებლებით სახანძრო სამსახურიდან, ბრიუსელის აეროპორტიდან და ანტვერპენ-ბრიუგეს პორტიდან; 3 ECTS.

Part of the University of Antwerp's Antwerp Winter University, this intensive week (1–5 February 2027) explores how organisations anticipate, manage and learn from complex crises, from pandemics to operational disruptions. It combines crisis communication, decision-making under pressure, organisational resilience and network governance with guest lectures from crisis professionals, and participants work in groups on realistic crisis scenarios, presenting a governance strategy on the final day.

The school is designed for master's students and professionals working in, or aspiring to, crisis management roles, in public administration, emergency services, business or research. It takes place at the city-centre Stadscampus; successful completion (full participation and the group assignment) earns 3 ECTS credits and a micro-credential. Applications are reviewed by the academic committee.

about.en:
This third edition of the UCSIA winter school, 'Dignity Amidst Despair: Migration Challenging European Solidarity', runs from 1 to 5 February 2027 in Antwerp. Experts from philosophy, history, law and political science examine solidarity and human dignity, EU social rights and instruments for migrating workers, and the politics of EU migration and asylum policy. Participants travel to Brussels to meet policymakers, work with migrant-support organisations in Antwerp, and present their own findings at the end of the week.

It is designed for PhD candidates and final-year master's students from any discipline, and young professionals with a master's degree are also encouraged to apply; the organisers aim for an interdisciplinary, intercultural group. Good English is required. Successful completion can be recognised with 3 ECTS credits.

about.en:
Run by the University of Antwerp's Faculty of Law with Roma Tre University, this course examines how law, policy and governance shape food production, circulation and consumption, and how they connect to food insecurity, health, climate change, labour and human rights. The first module is an academic week in Antwerp (1–5 February 2027); the second is a practitioner-based week in Rome (five days in late June/early July 2027, to be confirmed) with visits to the UN Rome-Based Agencies (FAO, IFAD, WFP), NGOs and EU representatives.

It is designed for undergraduates, master's students and PhD candidates interested in food law and policy, and for professionals from food-related sectors. Participants are expected to attend both modules; a limited number of hybrid places let students with limited means follow the Antwerp module online.

The Sustainable City summer school (28 June – 2 July 2027) brings together city experts, practitioners and academics to look at how cities are changing to protect sustainable living conditions for all. Seminars and lectures by sociologists, planners, economists, historians and ecologists cover water and air quality, energy, circularity and biodiversity and how they interact with social inequality; participants visit innovative projects in Antwerp and finish with a group project on a real urban sustainability challenge.

It is aimed at master's students, PhD students and professionals in urban studies and related fields, who should hold a relevant bachelor's degree and show an interest in urban sustainability. Teaching is at the University of Antwerp's city-centre campus, and successful completion can earn ECTS credits.

about.en:
The Centre for the Evaluation of Vaccination at the University of Antwerp runs this annual summer school to fill a gap in many medical curricula. From 28 June to 5 July 2027, lecturers from across Europe teach vaccine-preventable infectious diseases, vaccine immunology, immunisation programmes, vaccine safety and how to communicate about vaccines, alongside practical training in administering vaccines. The week ends with a group task, and a social programme is organised by Antwerp medical students (EMSA).

It is designed for undergraduate and postgraduate (para-)medical students and PhD students, with a particular focus on the WHO European region, which includes Georgia. Places are capped at 50, with selection balanced by gender and nationality, and scholarships are available for undergraduate students from the WHO European region. Unusually, the fee includes accommodation and all meals on course days. ECTS credits can be awarded on completion.

Using Almería's intensive greenhouse horticulture as a case, it explores the history of water management, labour migration and the shift to renewable energy, through in-class seminars on relational ethics and the social embeddedness of markets, bus excursions, a visit to the Alcazaba and conversations with people who live and work in the region.

The school is designed for master's students, PhD students and professionals interested in environmental or health humanities, environmental politics, social justice or bioethics; applicants need at least two completed years of higher education in a relevant field. deadline_note: University of Antwerp: applications accepted until 13 May 2027 unless the school fills earlier; early-bird fee for applications by 1 February 2027 (paid by 15 February).

summary.en: A five-day summer school on children's and young adult literature, themed 'Body and Mind' in 2027, with lectures, interactive workshops, two excursions and a chance for PhD students to present their research.
summary.ka: ხუთდღიანი საზაფხულო სკოლა საბავშვო და მოზარდთა ლიტერატურაზე, 2027 წლის თემით „სხეული და გონება“ — ლექციები, ინტერაქტიული ვორქშოფები, ორი ექსკურსია და დოქტორანტებისთვის კვლევის წარდგენის შესაძლებლობა.
summary.ar: مدرسة صيفية لمدة خمسة أيام حول أدب الأطفال واليافعين، بموضوع «الجسد والعقل» لعام 2027، تضم محاضرات وورش عمل تفاعلية ورحلتين وفرصة لطلاب الدكتوراه لعرض أبحاثهم.

about.en:
The University of Antwerp's Children's Literature Summer School (28 June – 2 July 2027) is devoted to the theme 'Body and Mind', approached from several disciplinary perspectives. Students attend lectures by specialists in children's and young adult literature, take part in interactive workshops and two excursions, and learn alongside an international group whose diversity is treated as part of the course.

It mainly targets master's and PhD students, but senior researchers and professionals interested in children's literature studies are also welcome; participants must have completed at least three full years of undergraduate study. PhD students can present their projects or give a 20-minute paper in two dedicated workshops. Applying by 1 February 2027 secures the early-bird fee.

en: 2027 theme 'Body and Mind'
Workshops where PhD students can present papers
Early-bird fee for applications by 1 February 2027

eligibility.en: Master's and PhD students, researchers and professionals in children's literature or related fields who have completed at least 3 years of undergraduate study; good English. All nationalities.

en: Read the programme page
Apply on Mobility Online (by 1 February 2027 for the early-bird rate, at the latest 13 May 2027)
PhD students: indicate if you want to present a paper
Pay the fee and arrange travel and accommodation

costs.en: Early bird (apply by 1 Feb, pay by 15 Feb 2027): EUR 520 for master's/PhD students, EUR 600 others. Regular fee: EUR 650. UAntwerp students get EUR 150 off. Includes coffee breaks, 5 lunches, 2 excursions and a banquet; travel and accommodation not included.

score_reason: Niche but open 2027 summer school; advanced students only.

org: University of Antwerp – Antwerp Summer and Winter University

name.en: Responsible Fashion Management Summer School 2027 (Antwerp & Paris)
name.ka: საზაფხულო სკოლა „პასუხისმგებლიანი მოდის მენეჯმენტი“ 2027 (ანტვერპენი და პარიზი)
name.ar: المدرسة الصيفية «الإدارة المسؤولة للأزياء» 2027 (أنتويرب وباريس)

duration.en: 8 days over two weeks (28 June – 7 July 2027)
duration.ka: 8 დღე ორ კვირაში (2027 წლის 28 ივნისი – 7 ივლისი)
duration.ar: 8 أيام على مدى أسبوعين (28 يونيو – 7 يوليو 2027)

deadline_note: University of Antwerp: applications accepted until 13 May 2027; early-bird student fee for applications submitted by 1 April 2027.

summary.en: An industry-focused summer school on sustainability and entrepreneurship in fashion, with sessions in Antwerp's independent fashion scene (28 June – 2 July) and Paris luxury houses (5–7 July 2027).
summary.ka: ინდუსტრიაზე ორიენტირებული საზაფხულო სკოლა მოდის სფეროში მდგრადობასა და მეწარმეობაზე — სესიები ანტვერპენის დამოუკიდებელ მოდის სცენაზე (28 ივნისი – 2 ივლისი) და პარიზის ფუფუნების ბრენდებთან (2027 წლის 5–7 ივლისი).
summary.ar: مدرسة صيفية موجهة نحو الصناعة حول الاستدامة وريادة الأعمال في الأزياء، بجلسات في مشهد الأزياء المستقل في أنتويرب (28 يونيو – 2 يوليو) ودور الأزياء الفاخرة في باريس (5–7 يوليو 2027).

about.en:
This University of Antwerp summer school combines Antwerp's pioneering independent fashion ecosystem with Parisian luxury heritage. The Antwerp week (28 June – 2 July 2027) and the Paris sessions (5–7 July 2027) look at how fashion businesses respond to environmental, social and economic challenges through sustainability, entrepreneurship and responsible management, with workshops, group discussions and real-world cases from industry.

It is designed for fashion professionals, entrepreneurs and third-year bachelor's, master's and PhD students who want to drive positive change in the industry, and values the exchange between academia and practice. Participants arrange and pay for their own accommodation and travel, including the trip from Antwerp to Paris.

en: Sessions in both Antwerp and Paris
Industry-led cases on sustainable and luxury fashion
Open to 3rd-year bachelor's students upwards and professionals

eligibility.en: Third-year bachelor's, master's and PhD students and fashion professionals/entrepreneurs; good English. All nationalities; check Schengen visa needs.

en: Read the programme page
Apply on Mobility Online by 1 April 2027 for the early-bird student fee (final deadline 13 May 2027)
Wait for selection
Pay the fee and arrange accommodation in Antwerp and Paris

costs.en: Students: EUR 990 early bird (by 1 April 2027) or EUR 1,200 regular; professionals EUR 2,000; UAntwerp students EUR 150 less. Includes course material, lunches, receptions and social activities; accommodation and all transport (including Antwerp–Paris) not included.

score_reason: Open 2027 programme with industry access; relatively costly.

org: University of Antwerp – Antwerp Summer and Winter University

name.ar: مدرسة أنتويرب الصيفية لتاريخ السينما 2027

deadline_note: University of Antwerp: applications accepted until 10 May 2027 unless full; early-bird fee for applications before 31 March 2027.

summary.en: A seven-day film history summer school with around twenty rare archival screenings in a cinema, lectures and seminars; the 2027 theme is 'Hollywood's Other Stars: Difference and the Business of Stardom'.
summary.ka: შვიდდღიანი კინოს ისტორიის საზაფხულო სკოლა დაახლოებით ოცი იშვიათი საარქივო ჩვენებით კინოთეატრში, ლექციებითა და სემინარებით; 2027 წლის თემაა „ჰოლივუდის სხვა ვარსკვლავები: განსხვავებულობა და ვარსკვლავობის ბიზნესი“.
summary.ar: مدرسة صيفية لتاريخ السينما لمدة سبعة أيام تضم نحو عشرين عرضًا أرشيفيًا نادرًا في دار سينما ومحاضرات وحلقات نقاش؛ موضوع 2027 هو «نجوم هوليوود الآخرون: الاختلاف وتجارة النجومية».

about.en:
The University of Antwerp's Film History summer school (4–10 July 2027) takes place at De Studio – De Cinema in Antwerp. Each edition is built around two themes: in 2027 the first is 'Hollywood's Other Stars: Difference and the Business of Stardom in Classical Hollywood Cinema', with a second strand still to be announced. Around twenty rare archival films are screened in proper cinema conditions, combined with expert lectures, in-depth seminars and discussion with scholars, critics and students from around the world.

The school is designed for master's and PhD students in film and media studies or related disciplines, and for film professionals with a strong interest in film history; participants need bachelor-level knowledge of film history and theory.

en: About 20 rare archival screenings in a real cinema
2027 focus on classical Hollywood stardom and difference
Small international group of scholars and students

eligibility.en: Master's and PhD students in film/media studies or related fields and film professionals, with bachelor-level knowledge of film history and theory; good English. All nationalities.

en: Read the programme page
Apply on Mobility Online before 31 March 2027 for the early-bird fee (final deadline 10 May 2027)
Pay the fee once accepted
Arrange travel and accommodation

costs.en: External participants: EUR 500 early bird (before 31 March 2027) or EUR 600 regular; UAntwerp students EUR 80. Includes course material, coffee breaks, lunches, opening dinner and closing reception; travel, accommodation and dinners not included.

score_reason: Open 2027 edition; specialised, postgraduate audience.

org: The Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU)

name.ka: ჰონგ-კონგის პოლიტექნიკური უნივერსიტეტის საერთაშორისო საზაფხულო სკოლა 2027
name.ar: المدرسة الصيفية الدولية في جامعة هونغ كونغ للفنون التطبيقية 2027

deadline_note: Estimated from 2026 pattern: the 2026 application for non-local fee-paying students opened 2 January and closed 6 April 2026 (exchange-partner nominations by 10 March). 2027 dates not yet published.

summary.en: A month-long credit-bearing summer school in Hong Kong: one 3-credit English-taught subject (39 contact hours) plus enrichment activities, local tours and a buddy programme, for students who have completed their first university year.
summary.ka: ერთთვიანი კრედიტიანი საზაფხულო სკოლა ჰონგ-კონგში: ერთი 3-კრედიტიანი ინგლისურენოვანი საგანი (39 საკონტაქტო საათი), დამატებითი აქტივობები, ადგილობრივი ტურები და ბადი-პროგრამა სტუდენტებისთვის, რომლებმაც უნივერსიტეტის პირველი წელი დაასრულეს.
summary.ar: مدرسة صيفية معتمدة لمدة شهر في هونغ كونغ: مادة واحدة بثلاث ساعات معتمدة تُدرّس بالإنجليزية (39 ساعة تدريس) مع أنشطة إثرائية وجولات محلية وبرنامج رفيق، للطلاب الذين أتموا سنتهم الجامعية الأولى.

about.en:
PolyU's International Summer School brings students from around the world to its Hung Hom campus each July. Each participant takes one 3-credit subject (39 contact hours, taught in English, with attendance, assessments and a final exam) chosen from a list across PolyU's faculties, and joins enrichment activities, local tours, a research-education talk with faculty, a buddy programme with PolyU students and a closing party. In 2026 the programme ran from orientation on 6 July to closing on 30 July, with halls open 3 July – 7 August; a free transcript is issued for credit transfer.

Non-local fee-paying students must have completed the first year of their university studies by the start, be in good academic standing and show English at TOEFL iBT 80 / IELTS 6.0 or equivalent (waivers for some qualifications). Students at PolyU exchange partner universities are nominated by their home university and have the programme and housing fees waived.

en: One credit-bearing subject taught in English
Enrichment activities, tours and a PolyU buddy
Fees waived for students from PolyU exchange partners

eligibility.en: University students of any nationality who have completed their first year by the start and are in good academic standing; IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL iBT 80 or equivalent (waived for some qualifications such as GCSE/IGCSE English grade C or IB English grade 4).

en: Check whether your university is a PolyU exchange partner (if so, apply via its exchange coordinator)
Otherwise apply online as a non-local fee-paying student when the 2027 application opens (expected early January)
Upload transcript and English proof before the deadline (6 April in 2026)
Pay the programme fee and reserve optional on-campus housing
Apply for the Hong Kong student visa with PolyU's support

costs.en: 2026 rates (2027 TBC): programme fee HK$17,000 (about US$2,185) for one subject incl. enrichment activities and student visa application; optional on-campus housing HK$5,000 (about US$643). Programme and housing fees waived for PolyU exchange-partner students (HK$550 admin fee). Flights extra.

score_reason: Established annual summer school; 2027 dates estimated from 2026.

org: Middlebury College – Middlebury Language Schools

name.ar: مدارس ميدلبري للغات صيف 2027 (برامج الانغماس اللغوي)

deadline_note: Middlebury: application opens 2 November 2026. Priority deadline 15 November 2026 (decision by 15 December); later rounds 1 February, 15 March and final 15 May 2027. Merit fellowships (Fellows for Peace, Kress, Conflict Transformation) close 15 December 2026; need-based aid is first come, first served.

summary.en: Seven- to eight-week intensive summer immersion in one of 11 languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Hebrew, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish) under Middlebury's Language Pledge, with merit fellowships and need-based grants.
summary.ka: შვიდ-რვაკვირიანი ინტენსიური საზაფხულო იმერსია 11 ენიდან ერთ-ერთში (არაბული, ჩინური, ფრანგული, გერმანული, ებრაული, იტალიური, იაპონური, კორეული, პორტუგალიური, რუსული, ესპანური) მიდლბერის „ენობრივი ფიცით“, დამსახურებაზე დაფუძნებული სტიპენდიებითა და საჭიროებაზე დაფუძნებული გრანტებით.
summary.ar: انغماس لغوي صيفي مكثف لمدة سبعة إلى ثمانية أسابيع في إحدى 11 لغة (العربية والصينية والفرنسية والألمانية والعبرية والإيطالية واليابانية والكورية والبرتغالية والروسية والإسبانية) وفق «تعهد اللغة» في ميدلبري، مع منح جدارة ومنح حسب الحاجة.

about.en:
The Middlebury Language Schools, run by Middlebury College since 1915, offer intensive summer immersion programmes, mostly on the Middlebury campus in Vermont. Students sign the Language Pledge, committing to use only the target language for the whole programme, and live, eat and take part in co-curricular activities together by language; an eight-week programme such as Arabic (18 June – 13 August 2027) carries 12 semester hours of credit, and levels run from beginner to advanced.

Applicants are typically university students, graduates and professionals (adults); international applicants are welcome but need a US visa allowing full-time study, which Middlebury's ISSS supports after enrolment. Funding includes merit fellowships such as Fellows for Peace, Conflict Transformation and Kress fellowships (deadline 15 December 2026) and partial need-based grants (up to US$7,200 for Arabic) awarded first come, first served, so applying by the 15 November priority deadline matters.

en: 11 languages, full immersion under the Language Pledge
12 semester credits for 8-week programmes
Merit fellowships and need-based grants; international students welcome

eligibility.en: Adult learners (normally university students, graduates and professionals) of any nationality; non-US students need a valid US visa status allowing full-time study. Specific fellowships have their own criteria.

en: Choose your language and level and read its Dates and Fees page
Apply online from 2 November 2026 (priority deadline 15 November)
After submitting, use the emailed links for merit fellowships (by 15 December 2026) and the need-based aid portal
Pay the enrolment deposit after admission/aid decisions
Request visa documents from ISSS (aim by 1 May 2027)

costs.en: Example (Arabic 8-week, summer 2027): cost of attendance US$16,920 = tuition US$11,400 + housing and food US$5,520; books and personal costs extra; travel not included. Need-based grants up to US$7,200 (Arabic); merit fellowships available.

score_reason: Prestigious immersion summer schools with fellowships; 2027 cycle about to open.

org: Rotary Club of Perugia with the University for Foreigners of Perugia

name.en: Rotary Club of Perugia International Youth Course Scholarships 2027 (Italian language)
name.ka: პერუჯის როტარი კლუბის საერთაშორისო ახალგაზრდული კურსის სტიპენდიები 2027 (იტალიური ენა)
name.ar: منح نادي روتاري بيروجيا لدورة الشباب الدولية 2027 (اللغة الإيطالية)

deadline_note: Estimated from 2026 pattern: the 2026 call (69th course, 6–31 July 2026) was published on 9 January with a 31 March 2026 deadline, as in 2025. The 2027 call is expected on the University for Foreigners of Perugia scholarship page early in 2027.

summary.en: Eight Rotary scholarships per year for foreign university students aged 18–25 to take a one-month Italian language and culture course at the University for Foreigners of Perugia, with free tuition, accommodation and meals.
summary.ka: როტარის რვა სტიპენდია ყოველწლიურად 18–25 წლის უცხოელი სტუდენტებისთვის პერუჯის უცხოელთა უნივერსიტეტში ერთთვიანი იტალიური ენისა და კულტურის კურსისთვის — უფასო სწავლა, საცხოვრებელი და კვება.
summary.ar: ثماني منح سنويًا من نادي روتاري لطلاب الجامعات الأجانب بين 18 و25 عامًا لحضور دورة شهرية في اللغة والثقافة الإيطالية في جامعة الأجانب في بيروجيا، مع دراسة وسكن ووجبات مجانية.

about.en:
Every July the Rotary Club of Perugia runs its International Rotary Youth Course (the 69th edition was 6–31 July 2026) in collaboration with the University for Foreigners of Perugia, Italy's oldest school of Italian for foreigners. The eight scholarship holders attend the university's Italian language and culture courses for the month and join activities organised by the club, such as visits to other cities and Rotary events, with the aim of fostering understanding between peoples.

The scholarship covers course enrolment, accommodation for the whole course and meals; students pay only travel, compulsory health insurance and personal expenses. Candidates must be 18–25, enrolled at a university, live abroad and hold a valid passport. Selection is made by the Rotary Club on the basis of the CV, and applications are emailed to the club using the official form (in Italian).

en: Tuition, accommodation and meals fully covered
One month of Italian language and culture in Perugia
Open to university students aged 18–25 of any nationality living abroad

eligibility.en: University students aged 18–25, of any foreign nationality and residing outside Italy, with a valid passport (and visa/permit if applicable). Georgian and Qatari students are eligible under these rules. Prior Italian not required by the call.

en: Watch the University for Foreigners of Perugia scholarship page for the 2027 call (expected January 2027)
Fill in 'Annex A' application form in Italian
Attach university enrolment certificate, a passport photo and your CV
Email everything to the Rotary Club of Perugia (address in the call) by the deadline (31 March in 2026)
If selected, arrange travel and health insurance

costs.en: Covered: Italian course fees, accommodation and meals for the whole course, Rotary activities. Not covered: travel, compulsory health insurance and personal expenses.

score_reason: Fully funded (except travel) language month with very broad eligibility; only 8 places.

org: Tel Aviv University – Lowy International School (Hebrew Language Studies Unit)

name.en: Tel Aviv University Winter Hebrew Ulpan 2027
name.ka: თელ-ავივის უნივერსიტეტის ზამთრის ებრაული ენის ულპანი 2027
name.ar: أولبان العبرية الشتوي في جامعة تل أبيب 2027

deadline_note: Tel Aviv University: Winter Ulpan application deadline 20 December 2026. Levels open subject to sufficient enrolment.

summary.en: A four-week intensive Hebrew course at Tel Aviv University, Sunday to Thursday mornings, from beginner to advanced level, for international students, professionals and others.
summary.ka: ოთხკვირიანი ინტენსიური ებრაული ენის კურსი თელ-ავივის უნივერსიტეტში, კვირიდან ხუთშაბათამდე დილით, დამწყებიდან მოწინავე დონემდე, საერთაშორისო სტუდენტებისთვის, პროფესიონალებისა და სხვებისთვის.
summary.ar: دورة مكثفة في اللغة العبرية لمدة أربعة أسابيع في جامعة تل أبيب، من الأحد إلى الخميس صباحًا، من المستوى المبتدئ إلى المتقدم، للطلاب الدوليين والمهنيين وغيرهم.

about.en:
Tel Aviv University's Hebrew Language Studies Unit runs short intensive Hebrew Ulpan courses in summer and winter. The Winter Ulpan runs from 21 January to 18 February 2027 on the Ramat Aviv campus, with classes Sunday to Thursday from 8:30 to 13:00, focused purely on Hebrew and covering speaking, listening, reading and writing for everyday, academic and professional use.

Courses may be offered from complete beginner to advanced, depending on enrolment, and are open to international students, professionals and anyone wanting to learn Hebrew in Israel. Participants can apply for TAU housing for short-term programmes, subject to availability.

en: Four-week intensive Hebrew in Tel Aviv
Levels from beginner to advanced
Option of TAU student housing

eligibility.en: Adults (international students, professionals, others) of any nationality interested in learning Hebrew; level placement on arrival. Check Israeli entry requirements for your passport.

en: Check the Winter Ulpan page and tuition page for current fees
Apply online via TAU International by 20 December 2026
Request TAU housing if needed
Arrange entry authorisation/visa and travel

costs.en: Tuition and application fees are listed on TAU International's tuition and funding pages (not stated on the programme page); housing extra; travel and insurance not included.

score_reason: Open winter language course with a December 2026 deadline; fee not stated.

org: Tel Aviv University – Lowy International School

name.en: Tel Aviv University Summer Research Program in the Sciences 2027
name.ka: თელ-ავივის უნივერსიტეტის საზაფხულო კვლევითი პროგრამა საბუნებისმეტყველო მეცნიერებებში 2027
name.ar: برنامج البحث الصيفي في العلوم بجامعة تل أبيب 2027

deadline_note: Estimated from 2026 pattern: the 2026 programme ran 3 June – 30 July with an application deadline of 1 April 2026. 2027 dates not yet published.

summary.en: An eight-week summer placement in a Tel Aviv University science lab, working as a member of a research team under experienced scientists and presenting findings at a final symposium.
summary.ka: რვაკვირიანი საზაფხულო სტაჟირება თელ-ავივის უნივერსიტეტის სამეცნიერო ლაბორატორიაში — კვლევითი გუნდის წევრად მუშაობა გამოცდილი მეცნიერების ხელმძღვანელობით და შედეგების წარდგენა დასკვნით სიმპოზიუმზე.
summary.ar: تدريب صيفي لمدة ثمانية أسابيع في أحد مختبرات العلوم بجامعة تل أبيب، بالعمل عضوًا في فريق بحثي تحت إشراف علماء ذوي خبرة وعرض النتائج في ندوة ختامية.

about.en:
Tel Aviv University, with about 400 labs and 125 research institutes, runs an eight-week Summer Research Program in the Sciences led by Prof. Ben Maoz. Participants join a participating lab as full members of the research team, carry out an independent research project under experienced scientists and present their findings at a final symposium to the group and faculty. In 2026 it ran from 3 June to 30 July; no formal TAU academic credit is awarded.

about.en:
Tel Aviv University's Advanced Epidemiology and Preventive Medicine Summer School offers short, intensive courses led by leading faculty and experts. In 2026 it ran from 12 to 22 July with three courses: Reproductive Epidemiology (sociodemographic, environmental and clinical determinants), One Health – Advanced Themes in Infectious Diseases Epidemiology, and Nutrition and Public Health. Each course lasts about a week (half-day sessions) and is worth 2 academic credit hours, so participants can combine courses.

The school suits medical, public health and life-science students, graduates and health professionals who want up-to-date training in epidemiology. Admission in 2026 was rolling, and partial scholarships were offered. The 2027 programme is expected in July again; check the page for the new course list.

en: 2 academic credits per one-week course
Taught by TAU School of Public Health experts
Partial scholarships available

en: Check the programme page for the 2027 courses
Apply online through TAU International (rolling admissions)
Ask about partial scholarships when applying
Arrange accommodation (TAU housing may be available) and travel

costs.en: 2026 tuition: US$900 per 2-credit course; partial scholarships available. Accommodation, travel and insurance extra.

summary.en: Six weeks living and studying at Exeter College, Oxford: two lecture courses taught through Oxford-style small-group tutorials (or a 1-to-1 Independent Research Tutorial), for university students with a strong GPA; a few part-fee scholarships.

summary.ar: ستة أسابيع من الإقامة والدراسة في كلية إكستر بأكسفورد: مادتان تُدرَّسان بنظام الدروس الصغيرة على طريقة أكسفورد (أو درس بحثي فردي)، لطلاب الجامعات ذوي المعدلات المرتفعة؛ مع عدد قليل من المنح الجزئية.

about.en:
The Exeter College Summer Programme is run by Exeter College itself, one of the oldest colleges of the University of Oxford (founded 1314). From 27 June to 7 August 2027 students live in college (en-suite rooms at the modern Cohen Quadrangle or historic Turl Street) and take two cross-disciplinary lecture courses taught by leading scholars, with teaching modelled on Oxford's tutorial system of small, discussion-based groups. Students interested in specialist research, a senior thesis or graduate school can instead work one-to-one with an expert on an Independent Research Tutorial. Evening lectures, study-skills workshops, formal dinners and a daily social programme complete the experience, and a transcript is issued.

Applicants must be in full-time higher education, be 18 and have completed at least one year of undergraduate study by the start, with a cumulative GPA of at least 3.6/4.0 or equivalent. Admission is rolling and competitive. The college offers a small number of part-fee scholarships and bursaries for admitted students with outstanding records (GPA 3.8+) and financial need (deadline 22 February 2027).

en: Run by Exeter College, University of Oxford
Oxford tutorial-style teaching or 1-to-1 research tutorial
Part-fee scholarships and bursaries for strong students in need

eligibility.en: Full-time university students of any nationality, aged 18+, with at least one completed year of undergraduate study and a GPA of 3.6/4.0 or equivalent; non-native speakers at non-English-medium universities need an English certificate. Scholarships: GPA 3.8+ and financial need.

en: Apply online (rolling) with transcript, academic reference, graded writing sample and English certificate if required; pay the GBP 60 application fee
Expect a decision within about a week
If admitted, apply for a scholarship/bursary by 22 February 2027 if eligible
Pay the programme fee by 13 June 2027 and apply for a UK visa or ETA

costs.en: 2027: application fee GBP 60; tuition GBP 4,495 (two courses, tutorials, academic support, transcript); accommodation GBP 4,355 (single en-suite room, weekday full board, formal dinners, social programme). Flights and insurance extra. Small number of part-fee scholarships/bursaries.

score_reason: Official Oxford college programme with 2027 dates, fees and deadlines published; expensive, some bursaries.

summary.en: A one-week philosophy winter school in Antwerp on the ethical, metaphysical and political status of dead human bodies and death-care practices in Belgium and beyond; EUR 200 student fee.
summary.ka: ერთკვირიანი ფილოსოფიური ზამთრის სკოლა ანტვერპენში მკვდარი ადამიანის სხეულის ეთიკურ, მეტაფიზიკურ და პოლიტიკურ სტატუსზე და დაკრძალვის პრაქტიკებზე ბელგიასა და მის ფარგლებს გარეთ; სტუდენტის საფასური 200 ევრო.

about.en:
Organised by the University of Antwerp's Centre for Ethics (Department of Philosophy, Faculty of Arts), this winter school (1–5 February 2027) examines the ambiguous status of dead human bodies, as object and subject, material and symbol, revered and despised, and explores the ethical, metaphysical and political implications in an international context that compares death-care practices inside and outside Belgium, including excursions.

It is designed for master's students and early-stage PhD students with a background in philosophy or death studies; familiarity with philosophical methods is required. Teaching takes place at the city-centre Stadscampus, and successful completion can earn ECTS credits and a micro-credential.

en: Small philosophy seminar on death and the body
Excursions on death-care practice
Low EUR 200 student fee

eligibility.en: Master's and early PhD students in philosophy or death studies (philosophical background required); professionals/researchers at a higher fee; any nationality; good English.

en: Read the programme page
Apply on Mobility Online before 9 November 2026
Receive the decision by 12 November 2026
Pay the fee and arrange travel and accommodation

costs.en: Students EUR 200 (UAntwerp students EUR 50); professionals and funded researchers EUR 250. Includes course material, daily refreshments, lunch on Monday and Friday and excursion transport; travel and accommodation not included.

score_reason: Open but niche and the deadline (9 Nov 2026) is very close.

No cost; travel bursaries; international applicants also apply for a paid research award.

about.en:
USEQIP is a two-week summer school run every year since 2009 by the Institute for Quantum Computing (IQC) at the University of Waterloo, Canada. It is aimed mainly at students one year away from finishing their undergraduate degree in physics, engineering, chemistry, mathematics or computer science. Lectures by IQC faculty cover quantum algorithms, error correction, cryptography, decoherence and the physical implementations of quantum computers; this is followed by more than 30 hours of experiments in IQC's labs, including NMR quantum control, entangled photon sources, superconducting devices, nanofabrication in the cleanroom and quantum key distribution.

USEQIP 2027 runs 31 May – 11 June 2027 with space for about 30 students, in person only. It is free and travel bursaries are available. Participants are encouraged to stay on for a paid summer Undergraduate Research Award (URA) with IQC researchers; international students are only considered for USEQIP if they also apply for a URA (one combined application).

en: Hands-on experiments with real quantum hardware at a world-leading institute
No cost, with travel bursaries
Can be combined with a paid summer research award at IQC

eligibility.en: Undergraduate students, ideally one year from completing their degree, in physics, engineering, chemistry, mathematics, computer science or related fields (all interested students may apply). Open to international students, who must apply for USEQIP together with a summer Undergraduate Research Award. Attendance must be in person in Waterloo.

en: Complete the USEQIP 2027 online application by 3 January 2027 (indicate URA interest; mandatory for international applicants)
Upload a CV, a cover letter (addressing USEQIP and the URA) and an unofficial transcript
Arrange one reference, due by 6 January 2027
Decisions are emailed by 31 January 2027; arrange a Canadian visa/eTA if selected

costs.en: Free; travel bursaries available. The optional Undergraduate Research Award is a paid summer research position.

about.en:
The Lisbon Machine Learning School (LxMLS) has run every July since 2011 at the Congress Centre of Instituto Superior Técnico (IST) in Lisbon. It combines morning lectures on machine learning, deep learning and natural language processing by well-known researchers from academia and industry with afternoon lab sessions where participants implement the methods in Python, plus a poster session and social events. The 2026 edition (the 16th) ran 20–25 July 2026, back-to-back with the ELLIS Doctoral Symposium.

The school is intended for graduate students and researchers in NLP, computational linguistics, computer science and statistics, and for industry practitioners; strong undergraduates with programming and maths background also apply. Admission is selective via an online application. A limited number of scholarships, funded by sponsors, cover the registration fee and sometimes travel and lodging for students worldwide who could not otherwise attend.

en: Lectures by leading ML/NLP researchers plus daily hands-on labs
Held at IST in central Lisbon with poster session and banquet
Scholarships for talented students from anywhere

eligibility.en: Graduate students (master's/PhD), researchers and industry practitioners in machine learning, NLP, computational linguistics, computer science or statistics; advanced undergraduates with solid maths and Python skills may apply. Open to all nationalities (participants handle their own Schengen visa).

en: Watch lxmls.it.pt for the 2027 call (expected early 2027)
Submit the online application form by the deadline (8 May in 2026); tick the scholarship option if you need funding
Admission results come about ten days later (18 May in 2026)
If accepted, register and pay (early or late rate) and book accommodation separately

costs.en: Registration (2026 rates, early/late): EUR 400/450 for students, EUR 450/550 for professors and public-institute researchers, EUR 650/750 for others; covers lectures, labs, lunches, coffee breaks and the banquet. Accommodation and travel extra. Limited scholarships cover the fee and possibly travel/lodging.

score_reason: Well-established ML/NLP summer school with scholarships; 2027 call expected early 2027.

about.en:
Emory University in Atlanta runs three summer programmes for high-school sophomores and juniors, with more than 100 courses taught by Emory faculty. The Pre-College Program offers two-week non-credit courses in three sessions (13–26 June, 27 June – 10 July, 11–24 July 2027), with residential or commuter options and campus activities and excursions. The Pre-Med Institute (13 June – 3 July 2027) is a three-week noncredit programme for students interested in medicine, with a single decision day. Summer College lets students take six-week, credit-bearing courses alongside Emory undergraduates (on campus for local commuters, or online).

Applications for 2027 open in December 2026. Pre-College decisions are rolling until the 3 May 2027 deadline; the Pre-Med Institute deadline is 1 February 2027. International applicants (anyone who is not a US citizen or permanent resident) are welcome and must show English proficiency if English is not their first language. Housing and meals are included in residential fees.

en: Courses taught by Emory faculty, from humanities to neuroscience
Dedicated Pre-Med Institute for future doctors
Residential college experience on Emory's Atlanta campus

eligibility.en: Students aged at least 15 by the session start who are currently in 10th or 11th grade, with a minimum GPA of 3.0. International applicants (non-US citizens/permanent residents) are welcome; if English is not their first language they need SAT ERW 700+ or ACT English 30+, or TOEFL iBT 104 / IELTS 7.5 / Duolingo (competitive around 130+). Summer College on-campus courses are for local commuters only; students from outside Atlanta take Summer College online.

en: Choose a programme and course (Pre-College, Pre-Med Institute or Summer College)
Start the online application when it opens in December 2026
Upload transcript, test scores (PSAT/PreACT/SAT/ACT), English proficiency evidence if needed and two teacher/counsellor recommendations; pay the USD 70 fee
Pre-Med Institute deadline 1 February 2027; Pre-College 3 May 2027; pay the USD 350 deposit once admitted

costs.en: 2026 fees: Pre-College 2 weeks USD 5,510 residential / 3,925 commuter; 3-week institute USD 8,264 / 5,874; 6-week credit courses about USD 6,485–8,589. Application fee USD 70; enrolment deposit USD 350. Residential fees include housing and meals. Financial aid for admitted students.

score_reason: Selective US university pre-college with pre-med track; 2027 dates out, internationals welcome.

about.en:
Wake Forest University's Summer Immersion Program offers week-long, career-focused institutes on its campus in Winston-Salem, North Carolina. STEM options include Artificial Intelligence, Biology Research, Coding and Computer Science, Engineering, Health and Exercise Science, Medicine, Neuroscience, Psychology, Regenerative Medicine, Sports Medicine, Technology and Women's Health; other institutes cover business, finance, entrepreneurship, law, policy, debate, filmmaking and writing. Students attend all five days, live in a supervised residence hall and earn a certificate.

The 2027 application opens on 1 November 2026 and admission is rolling until institutes are full, so applying early matters. International students are encouraged to apply and do not need a TOEFL score, but they cannot receive the need-based scholarships. 2027 week dates are published on the programme's Dates page.

en: Wide choice of one-week STEM and career institutes
Residential college experience with 24/7 supervision
Rolling admission from 1 November; no TOEFL required

eligibility.en: Current 9th–12th grade students in good academic standing with no school suspensions; home-schooled students welcome. International students are encouraged to apply (no TOEFL needed) but are not eligible for need-based aid.

about.en:
The UCLA Summer College Immersion Program (SCIP) gives academically advanced high-school students a six-week introduction to university life at UCLA. Participants enrol in approved UCLA undergraduate courses (earning UCLA credit) and attend co-curricular lectures, workshops and seminars on academic skills, research and the college application process, finishing with a certificate of completion. Variants include SCIP+ (research-skills focus) and eSCIP (online, from anywhere).

In 2026 the in-person SCIP ran 22 June – 31 July; UCLA's 2027 six-week Session A6 runs 21 June – 30 July 2027. International students who need a visa must apply earlier (1 April in 2026), enrol in two in-person SCIP courses to hold full-time F-1 status, and pay additional document fees. Admission is highly competitive.

Residential option in UCLA housing

International students are eligible; those needing an F-1 visa must take two in-person Session A6 SCIP-approved courses. All application materials must be in English.

The University of Miami's Summer Scholars Program is a three-week pre-college programme (26 June – 16 July 2027) in which current high-school sophomores and juniors take a university course for college credit, taught by UM faculty, in a range of subjects (past classes included forensics, microbiology and tropical marine biology). Students live on the Coral Gables campus, take part in college-prep workshops and explore South Florida on field trips and weekend excursions; almost 600 high-school students took part in a recent summer.

Alongside it, the two-week non-credit UM Academies (26 June – 9 July 2027) are open to 9th–11th graders, including the Shark Academy with UM's Shark Research and Conservation Program, an entrepreneurship venture challenge, and intensive English courses for English-language learners. Applications for summer 2027 open on 1 November 2026.

about.en:
The Da Vinci Engineering Enrichment Program (DEEP), run since 2003 by U of T Engineering's outreach office, brings high-school students with a strong aptitude for science and maths to the University of Toronto's St. George campus for week-long courses on topics usually taught in upper-year undergraduate or graduate engineering, such as AI, robotics, biomedical, chemical, civil and electrical engineering. Courses are taught by U of T master's and PhD students and run Monday–Friday, 9:30–15:30. More than 10,000 students have taken part.

In 2027 courses run in four one-week sessions between 5 and 30 July. Students apply once to be admitted, then register for up to four course weeks; a residence option on campus is available for each session (residence registration closes in mid-June). There are separate tracks for grades 9/10 and 11/12, and international students pay a higher weekly fee.

Open to domestic and international high-school students

eligibility.en: Students in grades 9–12 in the 2026/27 school year who have completed at least one year of high school. Grade 9/10 track: Grade 9 maths and science completed by June 2027; Grade 11/12 track: Grade 11 maths and science (chemistry and physics) completed. International students may apply (international fee rate applies).

Submit the joint DEEP/CREATE application and pay the application fee (CAD 50 Round 1 / 60 Round 2)

Optionally book on-campus residence before mid-June 2027

about.en:
Purdue Engineering's Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowships (SURF) programme, run by the Engineering Undergraduate Research Office (EURO), offers a 10-week immersive research experience. Fellows join a faculty-led project on Purdue's West Lafayette or Indianapolis campus, mentored by faculty and graduate students, in areas spanning engineering, computing, materials, energy, biomedical engineering and the sciences. The programme adds professional-development sessions on research skills and graduate school, and ends with every fellow presenting at the SURF Symposium.

For 2027 the programme starts with a remote week (31 May – 4 June), followed by in-person research 7 June – 30 July 2027 and the symposium on 29 July. It is a paid fellowship (the EURO site lists a USD 6,500 summer stipend). Undergraduates enrolled at Purdue, other US institutions and international institutions are eligible; international applicants must apply by 15 December 2026.

Open to undergraduates at international universities
Professional development and a final research symposium

Each participant joins an assigned research group in mathematics, physics, chemistry, biological sciences, macromolecular science or earth and space science, works on a thematic project under a host professor, and gives an oral presentation of results at the end. The programme also includes social and cultural activities with Osaka students and a one-day excursion, and is a good preview of the school's English-taught graduate programmes.

Tuition is JPY 57,600 (waived for nominated students from partner universities) and the bench fee is fully waived; a limited number of participants receive a scholarship of about JPY 50,000 or more.

Participants write a report on their findings and also attend academic lectures, visit world-leading national laboratories, tour Chinese cultural sites and meet USTC student clubs. Project lists are published on the FuSEP website.

The 2026 programme ran 22 June – 30 July with a deadline of 22 March 2026. Tuition, registration fees and on-campus housing are waived; excellent students receive a USTC Fellowship including a travel grant and meal plan, and outstanding participants are prioritised for scholarships if they later apply for USTC degree programmes.

Interns carry out an independent research project under a host principal investigator, receive training in research and scientific communication, visit labs to talk with PIs, join graduate lectures, journal clubs and seminars, and present at the NIG-INTERN Reports Symposium, receiving a certificate on completion.

Selection is extremely competitive (six students chosen from more than 1,240 applications for 2025). The 2026 internship ran 8 June – 17 July with applications 1 December 2025 – 5 January 2026. For 2026 NIG covered round-trip airfare up to JPY 200,000 and travel insurance, while interns paid guest-house accommodation (about JPY 70,000 for 39 nights) and living costs. Applicants of any nationality are welcome.

about.en:
The Institute for Integrated Cell-Material Sciences (iCeMS) at Kyoto University, home of Nobel laureate Susumu Kitagawa's porous-materials research, runs a five-week intensive summer internship for undergraduates enrolled at foreign universities. Interns conduct independent research in a host lab on topics integrating cell biology, chemistry, mathematics and materials science (with a special emphasis on self-assembly), take part in academic events and the iCeMS community, and finish with a final presentation. 2026 host faculty included Daishi Fujita, Aiko Fukazawa, Shuhei Furukawa, Mineko Kengaku, Susumu Kitagawa, Daniel Packwood, Easan Sivaniah, Jun Suzuki and Motonari Uesugi.

The programme is designed as a stepping stone for students who might pursue graduate study at Kyoto University in an iCeMS laboratory. In 2026 applications opened on 15 January and closed on 26 February; details on dates, support and documents are published in each year's application guidelines linked from the iCeMS internship page.

about.en:
Quantum in the Summer is the annual summer school of the University of Bristol's Quantum Engineering Technology Labs, one of Europe's leading quantum photonics groups. Over one intensive week on the Bristol campus, students start from classical optics through a mix of lab work and lectures and move on to classical and quantum computing, quantum algorithms and quantum key distribution. Instructors (Bristol quantum researchers) also share their experience of a scientific career, and there are evening socials.

The 2027 school runs 2–6 August 2027 for students aged 16 and over (16–18 by the start) who are studying maths and physics at A-level or equivalent and have completed the first year of that study. It is open to UK students and to international students who can obtain a UK visa. The school itself is free (lunches provided), but participants cover their own accommodation, travel and dinners unless they receive one of a limited number of bursaries, which cover accommodation, travel and food. Applications open in March 2027 and include a CV; applicants from groups under-represented in STEM are particularly welcome.

Free; bursaries cover accommodation, travel and food
Open to international students (with UK visa)

eligibility.en: Students aged 16–18 at the start of the school who have completed their GCSEs (or equivalent) and the first year of A-levels (or equivalent), are studying maths and physics, have strong mathematical ability and can attend the full week. Open to students from anywhere in the UK and to international students who can obtain a UK visa (e.g. a Georgian or Qatari student in the equivalent of grade 11–12).

about.en:
The Boulder School for Condensed Matter and Materials Physics at the University of Colorado Boulder is a long-running NSF-funded summer school with a new theme each year. The 2027 school (5–30 July 2027), coordinated by Roger Melko (Waterloo/Perimeter), Ehsan Khatami (San José State), Juan Carrasquilla (ETH) and Leo Radzihovsky (CU Boulder), introduces graduate students to the exchange between machine learning and many-body physics: foundations of ML theory and methods, statistical mechanics of learning, data-driven learning in classical and quantum systems, neural quantum states and applications to superconductivity, magnetism, atomic systems and quantum simulators.

Lecturers include researchers from Waterloo, Google, Leipzig, Los Alamos, UCSD, Perimeter, Flatiron/UBC and Munich. Students are expected to stay for the full four weeks. Accepted students pay a USD 400 registration fee; dormitory rooms are provided free (double occupancy by default) with weekday meals, and US-based students can get travel support, but students at universities outside the US must pay their own airfare.

Free dorm housing in Boulder; modest USD 400 fee
Strong networking for future PhD/postdoc work

eligibility.en: Primarily graduate students (and some postdocs) in condensed-matter, materials, quantum or computational physics and related fields, from any country. Students from universities outside the US are welcome but must fund their own airfare. Full attendance is expected.

Each week-long course is built around a design challenge inspired by one of the Faculty's engineering disciplines: students work through the engineering design cycle with practical activities, laboratory experiments and site visits, guided by current U of T undergraduate and graduate students. It complements the more lecture-based DEEP programme (the two share one application).

In 2027 CREATE runs in six one-week sessions between 5 July and 20 August (Monday–Friday). Admitted students can register for up to six courses; an on-campus residence option is available. There are separate tracks for grades 9/10 and 11/12, and international students pay a higher weekly fee.

summary.ar: دورات لمدة أسبوعين سكنية أو نهارية في جامعة تولين بنيو أورلينز لطلاب المدارس الثانوية، منها برامج معتمدة مثل Tulane Science Scholars ومستقبل الصحة العامة والعمارة، ودورات إثرائية في الهندسة والطب وغيرها. يتقدم الطلاب الدوليون بحلول الموعد ذي الأولوية.

about.en:
Tulane University's Pre-College Programs bring high-school students to its New Orleans campus for credit-bearing and enrichment courses. Programmes include the Tulane Science Scholars Program (hands-on STEM courses for college credit), Futures in Public Health (science, policy and communication of global health issues) and Explorations in Architecture and Design; the Tulane Summer Enrichment Institute lets students explore subjects such as engineering, medicine and sports without grades, and the Newcomb Summer Session focuses on gender and social change.

Residential students live on campus for a two-week session (in 2026: 14–27 June, 28 June – 11 July, 12–25 July), taking one credit course or two enrichment courses, with evening activities and weekend excursions in New Orleans; commuters can take one-week enrichment or two-week credit courses. In 2026 applications opened in early December with a 27 February priority/international deadline, and admission is rolling until courses fill.

en: Credit-bearing STEM and public-health courses at a top research university
Residential college experience in New Orleans
No application fee; need-based aid, including for international credit students

eligibility.en: High-school students: rising 9th–12th graders for enrichment courses, rising 11th–12th graders for credit courses; residential students must be at least 14. Graduating seniors are not eligible. International students welcome: TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo scores required if not a native English speaker; passport valid beyond the session and a US-based adult emergency contact (not an embassy) required.

en: Join the mailing list for 2027 updates and choose residential or commuter and your course
Submit the free online application (opened 5 December in 2026) with transcript and other checklist items
International applicants: meet the priority deadline (27 February in 2026) and include English test scores
Pay the 10% deposit within two weeks of acceptance

costs.en: 2026 tuition: commuter enrichment USD 995/week; residential enrichment USD 5,495 (2 weeks); commuter credit USD 2,595; residential credit USD 6,595 (2 weeks). No application fee. Need-based aid available (for international students, credit courses only).

score_reason: Accessible US pre-college with credit STEM options and aid; internationals welcome.

org: Rutgers University–New Brunswick, Pre-College Summer Programs

name.ar: أكاديميات رتغرز الصيفية لما قبل الجامعة 2027

deadline_note: Estimated from 2026 pattern: the 2026 application opened 5 January; the international-student deadline was 12 April 2026 (domestic 29 May, extended); academies ran in weeks from 12 July to 1 August 2026.

summary.en: One-week residential academies at Rutgers for 16–18-year-olds finishing 10th or 11th grade, in astronomy and astrophysics, engineering, design and prototyping, physical therapy, pre-law and more. Designed for US and international students.
summary.ka: ერთკვირიანი აკადემიები საცხოვრებლით რატგერსის უნივერსიტეტში მე-10 ან მე-11 კლასის დამამთავრებელი 16–18 წლის მოსწავლეებისთვის: ასტრონომია და ასტროფიზიკა, ინჟინერია, დიზაინი და პროტოტიპირება, ფიზიოთერაპია, სამართალი და სხვა. აშშ-ისა და საერთაშორისო მოსწავლეებისთვის.
summary.ar: أكاديميات سكنية لمدة أسبوع في جامعة رتغرز لمن هم بعمر 16–18 ويُنهون الصف العاشر أو الحادي عشر، في الفلك والفيزياء الفلكية والهندسة والتصميم والنمذجة والعلاج الطبيعي وما قبل القانون وغيرها. مصممة للطلاب الأمريكيين والدوليين.

about.en:
The Rutgers Pre-College Summer Academies are one-week, in-person residential programmes on the Rutgers–New Brunswick campus, designed for both US and international high-school (secondary-school) students. Each academy combines daily academic workshops, lectures, tours and activities led by Rutgers instructors with evening activities and events, under 24-hour supervision by programme and resident assistants. 2026 topics were Astronomy & Astrophysics, Engineering, Design Invent & Prototype, Physical Therapy (credit), Building Leadership Strategies (credit), Marketing & Product Innovation, College Readiness and Pre-Law & Mock Trial.

In 2026 academies ran in weeks between 12 July and 1 August; applications opened on 5 January, with an international deadline of 12 April. Class sizes are kept small. Students can attend more than one academy week (each charged separately).

en: Week-long residential academies incl. astronomy and engineering
Built for international as well as US students
Small classes and full residential supervision

eligibility.en: High-school students completing 10th or 11th grade, aged 16–18 (must be 16 before the summer), minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA and English proficiency (recommended TOEFL 79, IELTS 6.5 or Duolingo 105; otherwise an interview may be arranged). International participants need an F-1 or J-1 visa arranged through Rutgers Global after admission and must buy health insurance.

en: Check the Summer Academies Important Dates page for the 2027 cycle (opened 5 January in 2026)
Submit the online application with transcript and English proficiency evidence
International applicants: apply by the international deadline (12 April in 2026)
Once accepted, pay the USD 500 non-refundable deposit and complete visa documents with Rutgers Global

costs.en: 2026 total cost per one-week academy: USD 2,899 for non-credit academies (including housing and meals); credit academies USD 3,784–5,068 depending on residency status. USD 500 deposit counts toward the total. International students also pay visa, health-insurance and travel costs.

score_reason: Short residential academies explicitly designed for international students, incl. astronomy and engineering.

org: Syracuse University Pre-College Programs

name.ar: الكلية الصيفية في جامعة سيراكيوز 2027

duration.en: Up to 4 weeks on campus; 3–6 weeks online (summer 2027)
duration.ar: حتى 4 أسابيع في الحرم الجامعي؛ 3–6 أسابيع عبر الإنترنت (صيف 2027)

deadline_note: Estimated from 2026 pattern: the 2026 on-campus application opened 15 December 2025 with a financial-aid/scholarship deadline of 1 March and an application deadline of 1 May 2026 (rolling review; decisions in 2–4 weeks).

summary.en: Credit and noncredit college courses for high-school students at Syracuse University, living in a residence hall for up to four weeks, or online from anywhere. Students from 55+ countries have attended; international applicants welcome.
summary.ka: საკრედიტო და არაკრედიტული საუნივერსიტეტო კურსები სკოლის მოსწავლეებისთვის სირაკიუზის უნივერსიტეტში, საერთო საცხოვრებელში ოთხ კვირამდე, ან ონლაინ ნებისმიერი ადგილიდან. მონაწილეები 55+ ქვეყნიდან; საერთაშორისო აპლიკანტები მისასალმებელია.
summary.ar: مقررات جامعية معتمدة وغير معتمدة لطلاب المدارس الثانوية في جامعة سيراكيوز مع الإقامة في السكن الجامعي حتى أربعة أسابيع، أو عبر الإنترنت من أي مكان. شارك طلاب من أكثر من 55 دولة، ويُرحَّب بالمتقدمين الدوليين.

about.en:
Syracuse University's Summer College lets high-school students take a real college-level course and experience university life. Summer College – On Campus is residential or commuter, lasting up to four weeks, with credit and noncredit courses across many subject areas, plus residence-hall life, dining-centre meals and campus activities. Summer College – Online offers 3-, 4- or 6-week credit and noncredit courses with virtual events, accessible from anywhere in the world.

Students who successfully complete credit courses earn a Syracuse University transcript. Between 2018 and 2022 participants came from 50 US states and territories and 55+ countries. In 2026 the application opened on 15 December 2025 and closed on 1 May 2026, with rolling decisions; international students taking credit courses on campus need an F-1 visa (I-20 issued about three weeks after the deposit).

en: Earn Syracuse University credit or try a noncredit course
Residential college experience or online from anywhere
Students from 55+ countries

eligibility.en: Students aged 15+ by move-in. Noncredit courses: rising sophomores, juniors, seniors or recent graduates; credit courses: rising juniors, seniors or recent graduates. Non-native English speakers show proficiency (preferred TOEFL 85, IELTS 6.0, Duolingo 105, or English-medium schooling). International students on campus taking credit courses need an F-1 visa (not B-1/B-2).

en: Choose On Campus or Online and a course when the 2027 application opens (15 December in 2026)
Submit transcripts (at least one full year of grades), optional recommendation and English scores if needed; pay the USD 65 fee
Apply for financial assistance by about 1 March; final deadline about 1 May (rolling)
International credit students: pay the deposit, receive the I-20 and apply for an F-1 visa

costs.en: Paid programme; tuition, housing and meal costs vary by course and format (see the Cost and Aid pages). USD 65 non-refundable application fee. Financial assistance and scholarships available by the March deadline.

score_reason: Large, flexible pre-college with credit options and strong international participation.

org: Bentley University

name.ar: برامج ما قبل الجامعة في جامعة Bentley 2027

deadline_note: Official: the 2027 application opens 15 January 2027; rolling admission on a space-available basis until 15 May 2027. Seven sessions run from the week of 7 June to 23 July 2027.

summary.en: Week-long business, finance and data courses at Bentley near Boston: Wall Street 101 finance courses (some for credit), data analytics, quant risk management, AI in society and entrepreneurship. Residential (16+), commuter or online; international students welcome.
summary.ka: ერთკვირიანი კურსები ბიზნესში, ფინანსებსა და მონაცემებში Bentley-ში ბოსტონთან: Wall Street 101 ფინანსური კურსები (ზოგი საკრედიტო), მონაცემთა ანალიტიკა, რაოდენობრივი რისკების მართვა, ხელოვნური ინტელექტი საზოგადოებაში და მეწარმეობა. საცხოვრებლით (16+), დღის ან ონლაინ ფორმატი; საერთაშორისო მოსწავლეებიც.
summary.ar: دورات لمدة أسبوع في الأعمال والمالية والبيانات بجامعة Bentley قرب بوسطن: دورات Wall Street 101 المالية (بعضها معتمد)، وتحليل البيانات، وإدارة المخاطر الكمية، والذكاء الاصطناعي في المجتمع، وريادة الأعمال. سكني (16+) أو نهاري أو عبر الإنترنت، ويُرحَّب بالطلاب الدوليين.

about.en:
Bentley University, a business university in Waltham near Boston, runs one-week pre-college courses for high-school students from 7 June to 23 July 2027. The 2027 schedule includes the Wall Street 101 series (Macroeconomics and Financial Markets, Stock Market and Investment Research, Trading Strategies, Global Finance and Trade, Personal Finance, FinTech Business Start-ups, several offered for credit), plus Data Analytics, Quant Risk Management, AI in Society, Pathways for Women in Math, Accounting Adventures, Social Entrepreneurship, and the business of sports, health, fashion and beauty. Courses run 9:00–17:00 with workshops, networking with Bentley students and faculty, and social outings.

Students aged 16 by 1 September can live in the residence halls (residential fee includes housing, meals, weekday activity transport and an airport shuttle); younger students can attend as commuters or take online Wall Street 101 courses. Applications open 15 January 2027 with rolling admission until 15 May. International students are welcome; those without two years of US high school must show English proficiency.

en: Hands-on finance, data analytics and quant courses
Residential option with airport shuttle; online option
Some Wall Street 101 courses earn college credit

eligibility.en: High-school students; must be 16 by 1 September 2027 to live on campus (younger students may commute or study online). Applicants who have not completed at least two years of US high school must demonstrate English proficiency. International students may apply (Bentley does not support visa applications; scholarships do not cover travel).

en: Choose one or more 2027 sessions from the schedule
Create an account and apply online from 15 January 2027; pay the USD 75 application fee
Rolling admission until 15 May 2027; places are reserved only with full payment
Optionally request need-based scholarship (international students submit an extra financial form)

costs.en: 2026/27 listed tuition per 5-day course: online USD 1,490; commuter USD 2,450–2,800; residential USD 3,380–3,730 (housing, meals, activity transport and airport shuttle included). USD 75 application fee. Limited need-based scholarships (no travel funding).

score_reason: Practical finance and data pre-college near Boston; 2027 schedule and dates published.

org: Babson College (Babson Academy)

name.ar: الدراسة الصيفية في أكاديمية بابسون 2027

deadline_note: Official programme dates 12–30 July 2027. Key application dates are published on the programme page (Key Dates tab); an information session is held on 8 December 2026. No deadline is stated on the page we could read.

summary.en: A three-week pre-college course in entrepreneurship from Babson College, a business school known for entrepreneurship education, taken online or in person at the New England Innovation Academy with an added AI-for-innovation strand. For rising juniors and seniors worldwide.
summary.ka: სამკვირიანი წინასაუნივერსიტეტო კურსი მეწარმეობაში Babson College-ისგან, აშშ-ის წამყვანი მეწარმეობის სკოლისგან, ონლაინ ან ადგილზე New England Innovation Academy-ში, ხელოვნური ინტელექტისა და ინოვაციის დამატებითი მოდულით. მე-11 და მე-12 კლასელებისთვის მთელი მსოფლიოდან.
summary.ar: مقرر لما قبل الجامعة لمدة ثلاثة أسابيع في ريادة الأعمال من كلية بابسون، أبرز كلية أمريكية في هذا المجال، عبر الإنترنت أو حضورياً في New England Innovation Academy مع مسار إضافي في الذكاء الاصطناعي للابتكار. لطلاب الصفين الحادي عشر والثاني عشر من أنحاء العالم.

about.en:
Babson Academy Summer Study is an intensive three-week pre-college programme (12–30 July 2027) built on Babson College's Entrepreneurial Thought & Action methodology. All students take the Babson College course EPS 1110 Introduction to the Entrepreneurial Experience, working in teams on real-world business challenges linked to the UN Global Goals: three hours a day in class plus about five hours of team and individual work (around 40 hours a week).

It runs in two formats: fully online (classes 8–11 a.m. ET) or in person, hosted by the New England Innovation Academy (NEIA) in Massachusetts, with double-occupancy en-suite dorms, 24/7 supervision, evening activities, a Babson campus tour, local sightseeing and NEIA's AI for Innovation programme. An information session for 2027 is on 8 December 2026.

en: Real Babson College entrepreneurship course
Online or residential with an AI-for-innovation strand
Need-based financial assistance with fee waiver

eligibility.en: Rising high-school juniors or seniors aged at least 15 by the start date (no exceptions). English proficiency required (minimum TOEFL 90 or equivalent IELTS, Duolingo or Cambridge score) unless English is the native language or the school's language of instruction. Open to students worldwide; a computer, webcam and reliable internet are required.

en: Attend the information session (8 December 2026) and check the Key Dates tab
Complete part 1 of the Workday application and pay the USD 100 fee (waived if applying for need-based aid)
Complete part 2: school official uploads transcript; add English proficiency evidence and essays
Choose online or in-person (NEIA) format

costs.en: Paid programme; tuition for online and in-person formats is listed under 'Program Cost & Aid' on the Babson page. USD 100 application fee (waived for financial-aid applicants). Need-based financial assistance available.

score_reason: Entrepreneurship course from Babson College, online or residential; 2027 dates set.

org: Smith College Precollege Programs

name.ar: برامج ما قبل الجامعة الصيفية في كلية سميث 2027

deadline_note: Official 2027 dates: applications open 10 December 2026; priority deadline 1 February 2027; tuition-assistance and international-student deadline 1 March 2027; fee rises to USD 100 on 15 April; domestic applications close 1 May 2027.

summary.en: Residential one- and two-week programmes at Smith College for students entering grades 9–12: College Readiness, Creative Writing, Sustainable Futures, Women Gender & Representation and Theatre. International students welcome (18% in 2026); tuition assistance available.
summary.ka: ერთ- და ორკვირიანი პროგრამები საცხოვრებლით სმიტის კოლეჯში მე-9–მე-12 კლასში გადასული მოსწავლეებისთვის: კოლეჯისთვის მზადება, შემოქმედებითი წერა, მდგრადი მომავალი, ქალები, გენდერი და რეპრეზენტაცია, თეატრი. საერთაშორისო მოსწავლეები მისასალმებელია (2026 წელს 18%); სწავლის საფასურის დახმარება.
summary.ar: برامج سكنية لمدة أسبوع أو أسبوعين في كلية سميث للطلاب المنتقلين إلى الصفوف 9–12: الاستعداد للجامعة، والكتابة الإبداعية، والمستقبل المستدام، والمرأة والنوع الاجتماعي والتمثيل، والمسرح. يُرحَّب بالطلاب الدوليين (18% في 2026) مع مساعدة في الرسوم.

about.en:
Smith College, a residential liberal-arts college in Northampton, Massachusetts, runs summer precollege programmes that give high-school students a taste of college life (no college credit). The 2027 line-up is College Readiness (18–24 July; essays, public speaking and interview preparation), Creative Writing Workshop (3–16 July), Sustainable Futures (18–31 July; environmental activism and change-making), Women, Gender & Representation (18–31 July) and Theatre (18–31 July). Smith's Summer Science & Engineering Program runs separately (3–16 and 18–31 July).

Precollege programmes are open to students entering 9th–12th grade and do not discriminate on sex or gender identity. Admission is selective: applications open 10 December 2026, reviews are rolling from 4 January, the priority deadline is 1 February and international students must apply by 1 March 2027. In 2026, 18% of participants came from outside the US (including Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Moldova, Romania, Lebanon and Pakistan).

en: Small, selective residential programmes at a leading liberal-arts college
College-readiness, writing, sustainability, gender studies and theatre options
Tuition assistance open to international students

eligibility.en: Students entering 9th–12th grade in autumn 2027. International students welcome; Duolingo, TOEFL or IELTS scores required for international citizens and for students taught in a language other than English (including those taught in English for two years or less).

en: Choose a programme and apply online from 10 December 2026
Submit one academic teacher recommendation and the programme essay; pay the fee (USD 50 domestic / 75 international; USD 100 from 15 April)
International applicants and those requesting tuition assistance apply by 1 March 2027
Pay the deposit within two weeks of acceptance; final payment due 15 May 2027

costs.en: 2026 rates (2027 coming soon): e.g. College Readiness (1 week) tuition USD 2,795, deposit USD 699; two-week programmes cost more. Tuition assistance available; no travel funding.

score_reason: Selective small-college precollege with full 2027 dates and aid for internationals; deadline 1 Mar 2027.
